#!/bin/sh
# Minimal, no-sudo SpecStory installer (the fallback delivery channel).
#
# Downloads ONE static binary from GitHub Releases into a user-writable dir and
# verifies it against a pinned SHA-256 before use. Driven by env vars:
#   SPECSTORY_VERSION    git tag to install (e.g. v1.13.0); default: latest
#   SPECSTORY_BIN_DIR    install dir; default: ~/.specstory/bin
#   SPECSTORY_CHECKSUMS  path to a checksums file to verify against (optional)
#
# In the productized design this logic lives inside the `specstory` binary and a
# central installer; it is spelled out here only so the prototype is testable.
set -e

REPO="specstoryai/getspecstory"
BIN_NAME="specstory"
BIN_DIR="${SPECSTORY_BIN_DIR:-$HOME/.specstory/bin}"
VERSION="${SPECSTORY_VERSION:-latest}"

# Detect platform (matches the release artifact naming convention).
OS=$(uname -s | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
ARCH=$(uname -m)
case "$ARCH" in
  x86_64) ARCH="x86_64" ;;
  arm64|aarch64) ARCH="arm64" ;;
  *) echo "specstory-install: unsupported arch '$ARCH'" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac
case "$OS" in
  darwin) OS="Darwin" ;;
  linux) OS="Linux" ;;
  *) echo "specstory-install: unsupported os '$OS'" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac

# Download $1 to stdout using whatever HTTP client the machine has.
fetch() {
  if command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then curl -fsSL "$1"
  elif command -v wget >/dev/null 2>&1; then wget -qO- "$1"
  else echo "specstory-install: need 'curl' or 'wget' on PATH" >&2; return 1; fi
}

# SHA-256 of file $1, using whichever tool exists ("" if none).
sha256_of() {
  if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then sha256sum "$1" | awk '{print $1}'
  elif command -v shasum >/dev/null 2>&1; then shasum -a 256 "$1" | awk '{print $1}'
  else echo ""; fi
}

# Resolve "latest" to a concrete tag if no version was pinned.
if [ "$VERSION" = "latest" ]; then
  VERSION=$(fetch "https://api.github.com/repos/$REPO/releases/latest" \
    | grep '"tag_name":' | sed -E 's/.*"([^"]+)".*/\1/')
fi
[ -n "$VERSION" ] || { echo "specstory-install: could not resolve version" >&2; exit 1; }

FILENAME="SpecStoryCLI_${OS}_${ARCH}.tar.gz"
URL="https://github.com/$REPO/releases/download/$VERSION/$FILENAME"

mkdir -p "$BIN_DIR"
TMP=$(mktemp -d)
# shellcheck disable=SC2064
trap "rm -rf '$TMP'" EXIT

echo "specstory-install: downloading $VERSION ($OS/$ARCH)..." >&2
fetch "$URL" > "$TMP/$FILENAME"

# Verify against the pinned checksum when one is available. A mismatch is FATAL
# (never install a tampered artifact); a missing tool or entry only warns.
if [ -n "$SPECSTORY_CHECKSUMS" ] && [ -r "$SPECSTORY_CHECKSUMS" ]; then
  expected=$(grep " $FILENAME\$" "$SPECSTORY_CHECKSUMS" | awk '{print $1}')
  actual=$(sha256_of "$TMP/$FILENAME")
  if [ -z "$expected" ]; then
    echo "specstory-install: WARNING no checksum for $FILENAME; proceeding unverified" >&2
  elif [ -z "$actual" ]; then
    echo "specstory-install: WARNING no sha256 tool; proceeding unverified" >&2
  elif [ "$expected" != "$actual" ]; then
    echo "specstory-install: CHECKSUM MISMATCH for $FILENAME" >&2
    echo "  expected $expected" >&2
    echo "  actual   $actual" >&2
    exit 1
  else
    echo "specstory-install: checksum verified" >&2
  fi
else
  echo "specstory-install: WARNING no checksums file; proceeding unverified" >&2
fi

tar -xz -C "$TMP" -f "$TMP/$FILENAME"
mv "$TMP/$BIN_NAME" "$BIN_DIR/$BIN_NAME"
chmod +x "$BIN_DIR/$BIN_NAME"
echo "specstory-install: installed -> $BIN_DIR/$BIN_NAME" >&2

# NOTE: in the productized design this whole file collapses into a one-line
# `specstory hook <agent> <event>` call in settings.json, with the tiering below
# living INSIDE the binary. It is spelled out here only so the prototype is
# testable before the npm package and `specstory hook` subcommand exist.

# --- The one knob a tech lead turns: pin the team's version here. ----------
VERSION="v1.13.0"
NPM_PKG="@specstory/cli"
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

BIN_DIR="$HOME/.specstory/bin"
BIN="$BIN_DIR/specstory"
HOOK_DIR=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")" && pwd)
CHECKSUMS="$HOOK_DIR/cli/checksums.txt"

# True if the binary/command in $1 reports our pinned version (tolerates the
# tag-vs-bare-number mismatch: pin "v1.13.0" vs output "1.13.0 (SpecStory)").
have_version() {
  want="${VERSION#v}"
  got=$("$1" version 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}')
  [ "$got" = "$want" ]
}

# Resolve a runner, preferring an already-present binary, then trusted channels.
RUN=""
if command -v specstory >/dev/null 2>&1 && have_version specstory; then
  RUN="specstory"                                    # already on PATH
elif have_version "$BIN"; then
  RUN="$BIN"                                          # already in our cache
elif command -v npx >/dev/null 2>&1 && \
     npx --yes "${NPM_PKG}@${VERSION#v}" version >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  RUN="npx --yes ${NPM_PKG}@${VERSION#v}"             # (1) npm registry (Node present)
elif SPECSTORY_VERSION="$VERSION" SPECSTORY_BIN_DIR="$BIN_DIR" \
       SPECSTORY_CHECKSUMS="$CHECKSUMS" sh "$HOOK_DIR/install.sh" >&2; then
  RUN="$BIN"                                          # (2) checksum-verified download
else
  echo "specstory-hook: no install channel available; skipping capture" >&2
  echo "specstory-hook: tip - 'brew install specstoryai/tap/specstory'" >&2
  exit 0                                              # fail open
fi

# Do the work. Output to stderr (keep the hook's stdout clean); swallow failures.
case "$RUN" in
  npx*) $RUN sync >&2 || echo "specstory-hook: sync failed (ignored)" >&2 ;;
  *)    "$RUN" sync >&2 || echo "specstory-hook: sync failed (ignored)" >&2 ;;
esac
exit 0

```

```text
1	# SpecStory Autopilot
2	
3	_Zero-touch AI coding-history capture for any repo, any agent, any machine._
4	
5	> **The north star:** a tech lead commits **one thing** to a repo. From then on,
6	> every teammate — on macOS, Linux, or WSL, using Claude Code, Cursor, Codex,
7	> Gemini, or Droid — has their AI coding sessions captured automatically. No
8	> install step. No `sudo`. No "did you remember to run specstory?" Nothing on
9	> the machine to set up. SpecStory becomes a property of the **repo**, not the
10	> workstation.
11	
12	This is the same shape as `.editorconfig`, `.gitattributes`, or a `pre-commit`
13	config: check it in once, and it "just works" for everyone who touches the repo
14	— except here the payload is *complete, durable history of how the code was
15	actually built with AI*.
16	
17	---
18	
19	## Why this is worth building
20	
21	Today, getting a team onto SpecStory means asking every developer to install a
22	CLI and remember to run it. That fails the way all "remember to" workflows fail:
23	unevenly, and worst for exactly the busy senior engineers whose sessions are
24	most valuable. The history you capture is only as complete as your least
25	disciplined teammate's habits.
26	
27	Autopilot inverts that. The unit of adoption becomes the **repository**, decided
28	once by one person. Coverage goes from "whoever opted in" to "everyone who
29	clones it." That is the difference between a tool and infrastructure.
30	
31	---
32	
33	## Design principles (the non-negotiables)
34	
35	These are not aspirations — every one was forced on us by a real failure or
36	finding during prototyping (see [What we've validated](#what-weve-already-validated)).
37	
38	1. **Fail open, always.** A capture mechanism must *never* block, slow, or break
39	   a developer's actual coding session. Offline, GitHub down, wrong arch, no
40	   download tool — every failure path logs quietly and exits `0`. The first time
41	   it breaks someone's session, the team rips it out forever.
42	2. **No `sudo`, no PATH surgery.** Install one static binary into `~/.specstory/bin`.
43	   Reference it by absolute path. Works on locked-down corp laptops with no admin
44	   rights. PATH manipulation is the #1 source of "works on my machine."
45	3. **Pinned and reproducible.** The whole team runs one version, pinned in a
46	   committed file. Bumping it is a normal PR. No "latest" drift.
47	4. **Invisible by default, observable on demand.** Steady state is silent. But a
48	   developer can always see that capture is active and what it did.
49	5. **Bootstrap ≠ capture.** Installing the tool and recording a session are
50	   different events that happen at different moments. Conflating them is the
51	   single most common design mistake here.
52	6. **One asset, many platforms.** A single static Go binary that runs on
53	   macOS/Linux, arm64/x86_64, glibc/musl. Distribution is "download one file."
54	
55	---
56	
57	## Dead-simple setup: three tiers
58	
59	The same engine powers all three. You pick the scope.
60	
61	### Tier 0 — Just me, everywhere (global)
62	
63	```zsh
64	specstory init --global
65	```
66	
67	Writes a user-level agent hook (`~/.claude/settings.json`, etc.) and
68	`~/.specstory/cli/config.toml`. Every repo you open in a supported agent is now
69	captured. Nothing committed anywhere. This is the "I'm a solo dev / I want this
70	on all my own projects" path.
71	
72	### Tier 1 — This repo, my whole team (committed)
73	
74	```zsh
75	specstory init        # run once in the repo, commit the result
76	```
77	
78	Scaffolds the committed enrollment (below), so **anyone** who clones the repo
79	gets capture automatically — the bootstrap installs the CLI on their machine on
80	first agent session. This is the tech-lead path and the heart of Autopilot.
81	
82	### Tier 2 — My whole org, many repos (GitHub App)
83	
84	Install the **SpecStory GitHub App** on the org. It opens a one-click enrollment
85	PR (Tier 1's files) into each selected repo, and keeps the pinned version current
86	with automated bump PRs thereafter. This is "I have 40 repos and I'm not editing
87	40 of them by hand." See [The GitHub App](#the-github-app).
88	
89	---
90	
91	## What gets committed (Tier 1)
92	
93	Only **declarative config** — no shell scripts:
94	
95	```
96	.specstory/cli/config.toml    # pinned version + behavior (repo-specific)
97	.specstory/cli/checksums.txt  # SHA-256 of each release artifact — the in-repo audit anchor
98	.claude/settings.json         # one-line hook per event → calls `specstory hook …`
99	.cursor/… etc.                # one stanza per agent the repo enables
100	.gitignore                    # ignores generated history/debug + per-user local overrides
101	```
102	
103	There is deliberately **no `bootstrap.sh` or `install.sh` in the repo.** All
104	imperative logic lives in the `specstory` binary (a `specstory hook` subcommand)
105	and in the delivery channels (the npm package / a central installer) — one
106	canonical copy each, never duplicated across repos. A bug fix ships in the next
107	release, not in N pull requests. The committed footprint is a few lines of config
108	plus a list of checksums; a teammate can audit all of it in under a minute.
109	
110	> The prototype repo (`specstoryai/hook-sample`) still carries `hook.sh` +
111	> `install.sh` because the `specstory hook` subcommand and the npm package don't
112	> exist yet. Those scripts are the *spelled-out* version of what the binary will
113	> do — a staging ground, not the end state.
114	
115	---
116	
117	## Architecture
118	
119	```
120	                   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
121	   teammate opens  │  Coding agent (Claude Code / Cursor / …)     │
122	   the repo  ─────▶│   • loads committed hook config from repo    │
123	                   │   • one-time "trust this folder" prompt      │
124	                   └───────────────┬─────────────────────────────┘
125	                                   │ fires hooks
126	                   ┌───────────────▼─────────────────────────────┐
127	        SessionStart  ──▶  bootstrap.sh  ──▶  install.sh          │
128	                   │      (ensure binary present, no sudo)        │
129	        Stop / End    ──▶  bootstrap.sh  ──▶  specstory sync       │
130	                   └───────────────┬─────────────────────────────┘
131	                                   │
132	                   ┌───────────────▼─────────────────────────────┐
133	                   │  ~/.specstory/bin/specstory  (cached, pinned)│
134	                   │   • reads agent transcript (JSONL)           │
135	                   │   • writes .specstory/history/*.md           │
136	                   │   • optional cloud sync (if logged in)       │
137	                   └──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
138	```
139	
140	### Delivery — getting the binary onto the machine
141	
142	This is the crux. The committed hook calls `specstory hook <agent> <event>`. If
143	the pinned binary is already present (on `PATH` or in `~/.specstory/bin`) it just
144	runs — instant. If it's missing, it installs through the most trusted channel
145	available, in order:
146	
147	1. **`npx @specstory/cli@<pinned>`** — primary. `npx` *is* download-cache-and-run:
148	   it pulls the right platform binary (the Go binary wrapped as platform
149	   `optionalDependencies`) from the **npm registry** (signing + provenance) and
150	   runs the `hook` subcommand. Version-pinned inline, no committed script, no
151	   `curl|sh`. The kicker: **Claude Code is itself an npm package, so Node/`npx`
152	   is already present** in any Claude Code environment — zero new prerequisite.
153	2. **Homebrew tap** (`brew install specstoryai/tap/specstory`) — **live today**
154	   (`specstoryai/homebrew-tap`). Works on **macOS and Linux/WSL** (Homebrew runs
155	   on both). For non-Node environments. Trusted, no sudo, auditable, standard
156	   upgrade/uninstall.
157	3. **Checksum-verified GitHub Release download** — the zero-prerequisite fallback
158	   (needs only `curl` or `wget`). The downloaded tarball is verified against the
159	   SHA-256 committed in `.specstory/cli/checksums.txt` before it runs.
160	4. **Fail open** — none available? Print a one-line `brew install …` hint and
161	   exit 0. The agent session is never blocked.
162	
163	**A GitHub App cannot perform this step** — it runs server-side against GitHub
164	and has no path onto a developer's laptop. Binary delivery is always local
165	(npx / brew / download); the App's role is enrollment only (below).
166	
167	#### Why this feels safe — the levers
168	
169	Independent of channel:
170	
171	- **Version pinning** — `@1.13.0`, a tag, a versioned URL. Never "latest."
172	- **Checksum committed in-repo** — the expected SHA-256 lives in
173	  `.specstory/cli/checksums.txt` (declarative, ~four lines). The artifact cannot
174	  change underneath you without the hash mismatching. A mismatch is fatal; the
175	  install refuses to run a tampered binary.
176	- **Registry provenance** — npm `--provenance` (Sigstore) ties the published
177	  package to the exact CI build; Homebrew inherits the tap's audit trail.
178	- **Signed + notarized binary** — Developer-ID signing + notarization on macOS
179	  (closes the Gatekeeper gap), cosign/Sigstore attestation on the artifact.
180	
181	Version detection tolerates the tag-vs-bare-number mismatch (pin is `v1.13.0`,
182	binary reports `1.13.0`).
183	
184	#### Status today
185	
186	Two of the three channels are real right now — before any new work:
187	
188	| Tier | Channel | Status |
189	| --- | --- | --- |
190	| 1 | `npx @specstory/cli@<pinned>` | ⏳ pending npm publish (the one remaining build item) |
191	| 2 | `brew install specstoryai/tap/specstory` | ✅ live — macOS **and** Linux/WSL; tracks stable |
192	| 3 | checksum-verified GitHub Release download | ✅ live & tested (macOS; glibc + musl Linux; arm64 + x86_64) |
193	| — | fail open | ✅ |
194	
195	So a clean machine already has two trusted channels (brew on macOS/Linux, the
196	checksum-verified download everywhere); the npx tier slots in on top once the
197	package is published. The prototype proves the chain degrades gracefully until
198	then — an unpublished `npx` falls straight through to the verified download.
199	
200	Resolution order in the hook: **already-installed → npx → brew → checksum-verified
201	download → fail open.**
202	
203	### Capture timing — the part that matters
204	
205	| Hook event | Role | Why |
206	| --- | --- | --- |
207	| `SessionStart` | **bootstrap** (install the CLI) | The transcript doesn't exist yet, so there is nothing to capture — but it's the perfect moment to guarantee the tool is present. |
208	| `Stop` | **capture after each turn** | Fires when the agent finishes responding; the transcript now has content. Continuous, near-live history. |
209	| `SessionEnd` | **capture once at the end** | Lower overhead alternative to `Stop` if per-turn syncing is too chatty. |
210	
211	A future refinement is starting a **background watcher** at `SessionStart`
212	(`specstory watch`) for truly live capture, with `Stop`/`SessionEnd` as the
213	guaranteed flush.
214	
215	---
216	
217	## Lifecycle
218	
219	**First session on a clean machine**
220	
221	```
222	clone repo → open agent → trust prompt (one time) →
223	  SessionStart: download v1.13.0 → ~/.specstory/bin  (≈1s, once ever) →
224	  …developer works… →
225	  Stop: specstory sync → .specstory/history/<ts>-<slug>.md appears
226	```
227	
228	**Every session after that**
229	
230	```
231	open agent → (already trusted) →
232	  SessionStart: version match → instant, no download →
233	  Stop: sync → history updated
234	```
235	
236	**Version bump (tech lead edits the pin, merges PR)**
237	
238	```
239	teammate pulls → next SessionStart: installed version ≠ pin →
240	  download new version once → continue
241	```
242	
243	Self-healing: delete the cache, corrupt the binary, switch machines — the next
244	session re-bootstraps.
245	
246	---
247	
248	## Cross-platform matrix
249	
250	| Platform | Status | Notes |
251	| --- | --- | --- |
252	| macOS arm64 | ✅ validated | Gatekeeper: see below |
253	| macOS x86_64 | ✅ (asset + detection correct) | needs notarization for clean machines |
254	| Linux x86_64 — glibc | ✅ validated (Debian) | |
255	| Linux x86_64 — musl | ✅ validated (Alpine) | static binary runs on musl |
256	| Linux arm64 — musl | ✅ validated (Alpine) | |
257	| **WSL** | ✅ by construction | WSL is Linux; the Linux binary + shim apply unchanged |
258	| Download tool | ✅ `curl` **or** `wget` | minimal images often have only one |
259	
260	**The macOS Gatekeeper item is the one true productization gap.** The released
261	binary is currently only adhoc-signed and fails `spctl` assessment; it runs after
262	a `curl|tar` download only because that path sets no quarantine attribute. To be
263	bulletproof on clean Macs (and survive MDM policies), the release binary should
264	be **Developer-ID signed and notarized**. This is a build-pipeline change, not an
265	Autopilot change.
266	
267	---
268	
269	## Multi-agent matrix
270	
271	The bootstrap is agent-agnostic; only the *trigger surface* differs. The engine
272	covers any agent two ways: native hooks where they exist, a fallback where they
273	don't.
274	
275	| Agent | Trigger surface | Mechanism |
276	| --- | --- | --- |
277	| Claude Code | `.claude/settings.json` hooks | ✅ validated (SessionStart + Stop) |
278	| Cursor | project rules / hooks | native if available |
279	| Codex CLI | project config | native if available |
280	| Gemini CLI | project config | native if available |
281	| Droid CLI | project config | native if available |
282	| _any agent_ | **git hooks** (`post-commit`, `post-checkout`) | fallback: `specstory sync` after the fact |
283	| _any agent_ | **`specstory run <agent>`** | fallback: live-wrapper model |
284	
285	The fallbacks matter: even for an agent with no hook system, a committed git hook
286	(activated once via `core.hooksPath`) still captures history. No agent is left out.
287	
288	---
289	
290	## The GitHub App (enrollment only — never binary delivery)
291	
292	To be explicit: the App **never** installs the binary on anyone's machine — it
293	can't reach a laptop. It operates server-side on your repos. The binary always
294	arrives locally via npx / brew / download (above). With that boundary clear, the
295	App turns Tier 1 into a fleet operation and adds an optional server-side half.
296	
297	**Enrollment at scale**
298	
299	- Install on an org or selected repos.
300	- For each repo, open a clean PR that adds the committed enrollment files. One
301	  review, one merge, done — no hand-editing dozens of repos.
302	- A repo is "enrolled" when that PR merges; the App can show enrollment status
303	  across the org at a glance.
304	
305	**Maintenance**
306	
307	- Dependabot-style **version-bump PRs** when a new pinned SpecStory release ships.
308	- A CI check (`specstory verify-enrollment`) that fails a PR if someone deletes or
309	  breaks the hook wiring — enrollment can't silently rot.
310	
311	**Optional server-side value (only if cloud sync is on)**
312	
313	- Receive cloud-synced sessions and provide an org dashboard: who's building what,
314	  searchable history, links from PRs back to the sessions that produced them.
315	- Annotate PRs with "this change came from these SpecStory sessions."
316	
317	**Security posture**
318	
319	- The App writes only the enrollment files; it never needs code-read access to do
320	  Tier 1. Cloud/dashboard features are strictly opt-in and scoped separately.
321	
322	---
323	
324	## Robustness & security
325	
326	- **Trust model.** Capture rides the agent's existing folder-trust gate (Claude
327	  Code: one "trust this folder" acceptance per machine, then hooks run; no
328	  per-hook nag). That one click is the entire per-developer friction, and it's a
329	  *feature* — it's the human reviewing what the repo will run.
330	- **Auditable payload.** The repo commits only declarative config + a checksum
331	  list — no executable script. A security-minded teammate can read all of it in
332	  under a minute, and the checksum pins exactly which binary may run.
333	- **Pinned + checksummed.** Pin a version (never "latest"); verify the release
334	  checksum (and signature once notarized) before executing.
335	- **No secrets committed.** Cloud auth is per-user (`specstory login`), never in
336	  the repo.
337	- **Offline-safe.** No network? Bootstrap fails open; the session proceeds; next
338	  online session catches up.
339	- **Idempotent + fast.** Steady state is a version check and an exec — no
340	  re-download, negligible overhead.
341	
342	---
343	
344	## Observability
345	
346	To avoid "is this even on?", a `SessionStart` hook can emit a one-line,
347	friendly confirmation into the session (via the agent's context-injection
348	output): _"SpecStory capture active (v1.13.0) — history → .specstory/history/."_
349	Deliberate, quiet, and enough to build trust without nagging. `specstory status`
350	gives the full picture on demand (enrolled agents, pinned version, last capture).
351	
352	---
353	
354	## What we've already validated
355	
356	Not theory — exercised end-to-end during prototyping (`specstoryai/hook-sample`):
357	
358	- **Auto-install via SessionStart hook** on a clean Linux container: specstory
359	  went from absent → `v1.13.0` in `~/.specstory/bin`, with no manual step and no
360	  sudo.
361	- **Trust model confirmed:** Claude Code recorded `hasTrustDialogAccepted: true`;
362	  after that single folder-trust acceptance the committed hook ran with no
363	  per-hook approval. `/hooks` showed the SessionStart hook registered.
364	- **Capture confirmed:** after a real exchange (`what is 2+2` → `4`), `specstory
365	  sync` produced correct, attributed markdown in `.specstory/history/`.
366	- **Cross-platform:** binary selection matches published assets for all four
367	  OS×arch combos; ran on macOS arm64, Debian (glibc), Alpine (musl), and Linux
368	  arm64.
369	- **Download robustness:** added `curl`-or-`wget` fallback after a clean
370	  `debian:stable-slim` (no curl) silently no-op'd — caught only because we tested
371	  on a genuinely bare image.
372	- **Fail-open:** every "nothing to capture" / "not logged in" path exited cleanly
373	  without disturbing the session.
374	
375	The two known gaps: macOS **notarization** for pristine Macs, and wiring the
376	**`Stop`/`SessionEnd`** hook so capture (not just install) is automatic.
377	
378	---
379	
380	## Build order
381	
382	Each phase is independently shippable and useful on its own.
383	
384	1. **Publish `@specstory/cli` to npm.** Platform-binary packages
385	   (`optionalDependencies`, no `postinstall`), versioned to the release, published
386	   from CI with `--provenance`. This unlocks the primary delivery channel.
387	2. **Add the `specstory hook` subcommand + `specstory init`.** Move the tiering

1	# Working with me through deadreckon — a guide for the coding agent
2	
3	**Read this before we start.** We are going to build new functionality using
4	[deadreckon](https://deadreckon.sh) as the supervisor. Your job is not just to
5	write code — it is to **coach me through writing a good goal and a good
6	definition of done (DoD) first**, because in deadreckon the DoD is the contract
7	that an independent, signed gate (`dr-gate`) checks. You write the code; you do
8	**not** grade your own work. I (the human) own the goal and the done criteria.
9	Help me make them sharp.
10	
11	---
12	
13	## 1. The model you're operating in
14	
15	- **Goal** = plain-English instruction for the coding run ("what to build").
16	- **Definition of done** = verifiable criteria, compiled to checks that
17	  `dr-gate` runs *after* the coding finishes. The coder cannot edit or fake
18	  these. This is the whole point: *the agent owns the coding, deadreckon owns
19	  the boundary.*
20	- Every run happens in an **isolated git worktree** off a **clean base**.
21	  Nothing touches the real project until I explicitly `apply`/`finish`.
22	- A run is only **VERIFIED** when `dr-gate` passes every required check and
23	  **signs** the result. Watch for **caveats** — the gate tells you what it
24	  could not independently corroborate (e.g. "agent created the target file
25	  this run", or a check it couldn't run).
26	
27	**The discipline I want from you:** push effort into *what "done" must be true*,
28	not into a perfect prompt. Vague criteria → the gate can't check them, or
29	passes with caveats. Sharp, executable criteria → an unattended run I can trust.
30	
31	---
32	
33	## 2. The workflow — walk me through these steps in order
34	
35	1. **Map the existing analog.** I'm building something *similar to existing
36	   functionality*. Before anything else, read the existing feature and tell me
37	   what you found (see the interview in §3). The existing feature is our
38	   template and our source of parity checks.
39	2. **Draft the goal** with me (§3).
40	3. **Draft the definition of done** with me (§4). This is the part that matters.
41	4. **Compile and dry-check it** — `deadreckon def-done check` should **fail**
42	   before any code exists. If it passes before we've written anything, the
43	   criteria are too weak. Tell me.
44	5. **Confirm the clean-base + scope preflight** (§6 gotchas), then run.
45	6. **Read me the verdict** — including gate count (e.g. `PASSED 3/3`) and every
46	   caveat. Don't just say "done."
47	7. **Apply** once I approve.
48	
49	Do not skip to coding. If I hand you a one-line goal, your first response is the
50	interview, not an implementation.
51	
52	---
53	
54	## 3. Goal-writing interview (ask me these)
55	
56	Because the new work mirrors existing functionality, anchor everything on the
57	analog:
58	
59	- **"Which existing feature is the template? Point me at the files."** Then go
60	  read them and summarize the pattern back to me (layers, naming, where tests
61	  live, error handling, how it's wired in).
62	- **"What is the same, and what is deliberately different?"** Make me name the
63	  deltas explicitly. The default assumption is *mirror the analog exactly except
64	  for these named deltas.*
65	- **"What conventions must it follow?"** (file layout, naming, lint/format,
66	  test framework and location, commit style). Pull these from the existing code,
67	  don't invent them.
68	- **"What is explicitly out of scope?"** Capture this — it becomes a negative
69	  criterion ("does not modify X").
70	- **"How will we know it works the same way the existing one does?"** Their
71	  answer is the seed of the parity checks in §4.
72	
73	Then write the goal back to me as 2–5 sentences: what to build, which analog to
74	follow, the named deltas, and the scope boundary. Get my sign-off.
75	
76	---
77	
78	## 4. Definition-of-done coaching — the heart of this
79	
80	Use `deadreckon def-done "<plain English>"`. It compiles English into
81	`.deadreckon/acceptance.yaml` (machine checks) + `acceptance.md` (readable) and
82	can generate helper scripts. Add criteria incrementally with
83	`deadreckon def-done add "<one more thing>"`.
84	
85	**Principles — hold me to these:**
86	
87	- **Executable, not aspirational.** Each criterion should reduce to a command
88	  that exits 0 (pass) or non-zero (fail). "Works well" is not a criterion;
89	  "`<test cmd>` exits 0" is.
90	- **Behavior, not implementation.** Check what the feature *does*, not how it's
91	  coded. Don't pin internal structure unless I say it's load-bearing.
92	- **Front-load the ambiguity.** Every "it depends" we resolve now is a failed
93	  unattended run we avoid later.
94	- **Beware self-grading.** If the coding run also writes the tests that judge
95	  it, the gate is weaker. Prefer that *I* specify the expected behavior
96	  concretely (exact outputs, specific cases), or that we reuse/extend the
97	  existing feature's test suite. The gate reports **"tests modified this run"** —
98	  surface that to me.
99	
100	**For "new feature that mirrors an existing one," propose this DoD skeleton and
101	tailor each line to our actual stack:**
102	
103	- [ ] **Builds / typechecks** — `<build or typecheck cmd>` exits 0.
104	- [ ] **No regressions** — the *existing* test suite still passes:
105	      `<existing test cmd>` exits 0. (This is your safety net — always include
106	      it.)
107	- [ ] **New behavior verified** — concrete, named cases for the new feature pass
108	      (exact inputs → exact outputs, or `<new test cmd>` exits 0).
109	- [ ] **Parity with the analog** — the new feature satisfies the *same* contract
110	      the existing one does for their shared surface (same response shape, same
111	      error handling, same edge cases). State the specific parity assertions.
112	- [ ] **Conventions** — lint/format clean: `<lint cmd>` / `<format-check cmd>`
113	      exit 0; new files follow the existing layout and naming.
114	- [ ] **Clean run** — feature runs with no errors / no console errors / nothing
115	      on stderr, as applicable.
116	- [ ] **Scope guard (negative criterion)** — does not modify `<out-of-scope
117	      paths>`; no new unpinned dependencies unless I approved them.
118	
119	Write each as one plain-English sentence to `def-done`, then run
120	`deadreckon def-done show` and read the compiled checks back to me so I can see
121	exactly what the gate will enforce.
122	
123	---
124	
125	## 5. Command cheat sheet (verified)
126	
127	```bash
128	# Author / refine the contract
129	deadreckon def-done "<what 'done' means, in plain English>"
130	deadreckon def-done add "<one more thing that must be true>"
131	deadreckon def-done show          # see the compiled checks
132	deadreckon def-done check         # dry-run the checks against the working dir
133	                                  #   -> MUST fail before we write code
134	
135	# Run the goal (auto-uses .deadreckon/acceptance.yaml when present)
136	deadreckon run "<the goal>" --acceptance .deadreckon/acceptance.yaml --yes
137	deadreckon run "<the goal>" --preview     # see the plan without starting state
138	
139	# Watch / inspect
140	deadreckon status                 # latest run + recommended next action
141	deadreckon attach latest          # live view
142	deadreckon show <run-id>          # raw state, traces, provenance
143	
144	# Land the verified result
145	deadreckon finish <run-id> --autostash --cleanup --no-confirm
146	# (or: deadreckon apply <run-id> --no-confirm, then cleanup)
147	```
148	
149	Run/DoD artifacts live under `.deadreckon/` (git-ignored) and each run writes
150	audit docs to `docs/RUN-*.md` (decisions, as-built, narrative) — read these to
151	explain to me *why* the agent did what it did.
152	
153	---
154	
155	## 6. Gotchas — check these before every run (learned the hard way)
156	
157	- **Clean git tree required.** deadreckon refuses to start from a dirty source
158	  because it needs a clean base to apply or roll back from. Before a run:
159	  `git status` must be clean. Commit or stash real changes, and **gitignore
160	  build artifacts** (e.g. `__pycache__/`, `*.pyc`, `node_modules/`, `dist/`,
161	  coverage output). A stray generated file *will* block the run.
162	- **Non-interactive flags.** Use `--yes` to confirm the run preflight, and
163	  `--no-confirm` for `apply`/`finish` — without them those commands stop and
164	  wait for input.
165	- **The gate is only as strong as the DoD.** If a criterion can't execute in the
166	  sandbox (e.g. a tool isn't installed there), the gate may pass *with a
167	  caveat* instead of truly verifying it. If a check needs a dependency, make
168	  installing/providing it part of the goal — don't let a caveat masquerade as a
169	  pass. Always read the caveats aloud to me.
170	- **Report the verdict honestly.** Tell me the gate ratio (`PASSED n/n`),
171	  whether it was signed, the changed-file count, and any caveat or "tests
172	  modified this run" flag. If a required check failed, show me the failing
173	  command and its stderr — don't paper over it.
174	
175	---
176	
177	## 7. What I expect from you in our first exchange
178	
179	When I give you the goal, respond with:
180	1. A summary of the **existing analog** after reading it (files, pattern,
181	   conventions, where its tests live).
182	2. The **clarifying questions** from §3 that you genuinely can't answer from the

185	   plain-English `def-done` lines, each tied to a concrete command where
186	   possible.
187	
188	Then we iterate on the DoD until `deadreckon def-done check` fails for the right
189	reasons, and only then do we run.

# Lore Skill Architecture - Complete Technical Summary

## Executive Summary: The Pattern

**Lore is a deterministic engine + agent synthesis system.** The engine parses transcripts into beats (intent → method → outcome), counts and caches patterns in SQLite, and exports evidence. The agent reads only that evidence, names/judges/deep-mines, and forges skills. **You can never hallucinate in the engine; the agent never reads whole transcripts.**

---

## 1. Deterministic Beats Architecture

### What are "Beats"?
A **beat** is the atomic unit of analysis:
- **INTENT** - one user turn / prompt (≤30 lines, text only)
- **METHOD** - everything the agent does until the next user turn: executed commands, files touched, tool types used, exit-code failures
- **OUTCOME** - labeled retroactively from the user's next turn (via regex classifiers):
  - `✓ success` - "ok", "perfect", approval language
  - `✗ corrected` - "no wait", "still wrong", steering corrections
  - `· neutral` - new task (most beats)
  - `end` - session closes

**The outcome trick:** Your own next reply is free supervision. No annotations needed.

### The Deterministic Pipeline (5 Phases)

```
Phase 1: PARSE BEATS (deterministic, zero LLM)
  .specstory/history/*.md  →  text walk  →  beat rows (no I/O during parse)
  ├─ extract intent (USER marker → intent_raw, intent_sig via verb+keyword)
  ├─ extract method (shell/read/write tools, commands, files, exit codes)
  ├─ accumulate into beats
  └─ retroactively label outcomes (beat[k].outcome = classifyOutcome(beat[k+1].opening))

Phase 2: INDEX (incremental, idempotent)
  parse → INSERT/REPLACE into corpus  (~/.specstory/lore.db)
  ├─ fingerprint = size + mtime + PARSER_VERSION (unchanged files skipped)
  ├─ session id = project_id + '/' + filename (stable across reorganizations)
  └─ author attributed: git add-author → path sniff → machine user

Phase 2d: FOUR CANDIDATE CHANNELS (SQL GROUP BYs)
  beats  ├─  COMMANDS (n-grams over executed cmds, grouped by gram)
         ├─  INTENTS (verb:keyword signatures, grouped by intent_sig)
         ├─  META (way-of-working detectors - read-only-diagnosis, reasoning-dial, etc.)
         └─  THEMES (semantic clusters - LLM lenses over conversational beats)

Phase 2b: CORROBORATION (strongest truth signal)
  Intent × Procedure co-occurring in SAME beats:
  "the user asked for X and the agent did Y, repeatedly" - reported with outcome rates
  SQL: beats ⋈ grams WHERE intent_sig = ? AND gram = ?

Phase 3: DEEP-MINE (per harness, cached)
  cluster → beats export (stratified: corrected first, success, recent neutral)
            → content fingerprint (from session_id, ord, start_line, outcome, n_cmds)
            → one MINER reads every beat + one ADVERSARIAL VERIFIER
            → dossier cache (keyed by cluster_key + fingerprint)
            → verified dossier replaces sampled version
```

**The state machine is implicit in the code flow, not explicit.** Each phase is triggered by the agent's control - there is no loop or state enum. The "beats" are materialized in `scripts/lib/beats.mjs` and cached in the `dossiers` SQLite table.

---

## 2. Local-Only vs Cloud/Online

**There is no "local-only" mode distinct from a cloud mode.** Lore runs entirely local:
- All parsing and counting happens in `scripts/lib/*.mjs` (Node.js, zero network, zero API keys)
- Corpus stored at `~/.specstory/lore.db` (one SQLite file, portable)
- No cloud backend, no external services
- The only network call is when the agent optionally spawns subagents (deep-mine / theme mining), which are HARNESS-SPECIFIC:
  - **Claude Code:** runs `scripts/deep-mine.workflow.js` (bundled Workflow script, parallel subagents via Claude Code's Workflow mechanism)
  - **Codex / others:** spawn their own parallel subagents with the same briefs
  - **Sequential fallback:** agent reads `beats` export and mines linearly (no subagents)

**What "local-only" likely means in your user's comment:** The Lore engine has **zero external dependencies** and zero hallucination vectors - it's pure parsing + SQL. That's why it's deterministic.

---

## 3. Input: Reading SpecStory Histories

### Paths and Formats
```
.specstory/history/*.md          ← default (current project)
.specstory/history/202X-*/…      ← nested by year/month (specstory-organize layout)
~/code/*//.specstory/history/    ← cross-project mode (--projects ~/code)
(any depth)                       ← --scan . finds all at any depth (monorepos)
```

### Parsing Libraries
- **Entry:** `scripts/lib/discover.mjs`
  - `walkMd(dir)` - recursively list *.md files (handles year/month nesting)
  - `readLabel(historyDir)` - stable project identity from `.specstory/.project.json` (git_id preferred)
  - `scanForHistories(root, maxDepth=6)` - monorepo discovery (skips node_modules, build, etc.)
  - `discoverProjects(args)` - resolves `--dir`, `--projects`, `--scan` into `{historyDir, id, name}[]`

- **Core:** `scripts/lib/parse.mjs` (pure function, fully unit-testable)
  - `parseSessionFile(text)` → `{agent, uuid, beats: [...]}`
    - Walks transcript once, segments at `_**User**_` markers
    - Extracts intent (≤30 lines), method tools, and outcome labels
  - `extractShellBlock(summary, body, line)` → `{cmds: [{cmd, line}], fails}`
    - Handles **4 command locations** (modern + legacy):
      1. Codex in-summary: `` `cmd` `` inside `<summary>`
      2. Claude single-line: inline-backtick body line
      3. Multi-line: bash/sh/zsh/shell fence (heredoc bodies skipped)
      4. Codex legacy "- command:" bullet (can be multi-line)
  - `headsFrom(cmd)` → `[head1, head2, ...]`
    - Splits chains (`&&`, `;`), strips env prefixes, unwraps `bash -lc`, drops noise
    - Keeps subcommands (`git status`) and project scripts (`./scripts/run.sh`)
  - `intentSig(raw)` → `"verb:keyword"` (e.g. `"build:run"`, `"write:commit"`)
    - Leading verb from `VERBS`, first salient keyword via `tokenize`/`STOP`

### Pattern Grammar
All patterns in `scripts/lib/patterns.mjs`:
```
SESSION_HDR         - <!-- <Provider> Session <uuid> (ts) -->
USER_MARK, TURN_MARK - _**User**_, _**Agent**_
TOOLUSE_OPEN        - <tool-use data-tool-type="T" ...>
SUMMARY_CMD         - backtick in <summary>
INLINE_CMD          - backtick on body line
FENCE_LINE          - ```bash / ```sh / etc.
HEREDOC_OPEN        - <<'EOF' marker (skip content)
BULLET_CMD          - - command: `[...]`
SHELL_TOOLS         - executor names (Bash, exec_command, shell, shell_command)
SHELL_EXCLUDE       - noise (LS, list_directory, TaskOutput, KillShell)
META                - fixed detector patterns (read-only-diagnosis, reasoning-dial, trace-code-paths, ...)
CORRECTED_RE        - "no|wait|still|wrong|..." regex
SUCCESS_RE          - "ok|perfect|great|go ahead|..." regex
VERBS               - ~200 action verbs (build, write, run, fix, check, ...)
STOP                - common noise words (the, a, to, for, ...)
NOISE               - recon commands (cd, nl, grep, sed, head, tail, ...)
COMMON              - universal commands (git, ls, cat, ...)
```

---

## 4. The Engine: Module Breakdown and Control Flow

### Entry Point
**`scripts/mine-skills.mjs`** - thin CLI dispatcher (272 lines)
- Parses `process.argv` into `ARGS` object
- Dispatches to subcommands
- Returns results to `process.stdout` / `process.stderr`

### Core Library Modules

| File | Responsibility | Key Functions |
|------|---|---|
| **patterns.mjs** | Format grammar + classifiers | `SESSION_HDR`, `TOOLUSE_OPEN`, `CORRECTED_RE`/`SUCCESS_RE`, `classifyOutcome()`, `tokenize()`, `redactSecrets()` |
| **parse.mjs** | Pure text → beats | `parseSessionFile()`, `extractShellBlock()`, `headsFrom()`, `intentSig()`, `sniffAuthor()` |
| **discover.mjs** | File discovery + stable project ID | `walkMd()`, `readLabel()`, `scanForHistories()`, `discoverProjects()`, `fileDate()` |
| **db.mjs** | SQLite schema + migrations | `openDb()`, `PARSER_VERSION`, `deleteSessionRows()`, `addRun()`/`listRuns()` |
| **indexer.mjs** | Incremental indexing pipeline | `indexCorpus()`, `pruneCorpus()`, `gitAuthors()` |
| **report.mjs** | Corroboration queries + scoring | `report()`, `status()`, `skillsInventory()`, `wantedKinds()`, scoring formula |
| **beats.mjs** | Span export, sampling, dossier cache | `exportBeats()`, `exportRows()`, `sampleBeats()`, `selectBeats()`, `stratify()`, `beatsFingerprint()`, `getDossier()`/`putDossier()/`renderDossiers()`, `putTheme()`/`listThemes()`/`renderThemes()`, `expandTheme()`/`growTheme()`, `renderForgePlan()` |
| **forged.mjs** | Registry (provenance + drift) | `addForged()`, `declineCandidate()`, `listForged()`, `checkForged()`, `inferKind()` |

### Control Flow by Subcommand

#### **`index --dir <hist> | --projects <parent> | --scan <root>`**
```
1. discover.discoverProjects(args)  → [{historyDir, id, name}...]
2. for each project:
     discover.walkMd(historyDir)    → [path1, path2, ...]
     for each .md file:
       fs.statSync → fingerprint (size + mtime)
       check db: is this (project_id/filename) known + unchanged?
       if no: 
         fs.readFileSync → text
         parse.parseSessionFile(text) → {agent, uuid, beats:[...]}
         db transaction:
           INSERT sessions row
           for each beat:
             INSERT beats row
             for each command head:
               INSERT commands row
               for each n-gram (n=2..4):
                 INSERT grams row
             for each META detector hit:
               INSERT meta_hits row
3. db.addRun('index', projects, summary)
4. stdout: "indexed N sessions (M unchanged) → ~/.specstory/lore.db"
```

#### **`report [--min-sessions N] [--top N] [--days N] [--kind cmd,task,meta,corr] [--filter S]`**
```
1. SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sessions → scope (projects, sessions)
2. For each wanted kind:
   - RUNBOOKS:     GROUP BY gram, count distinct sessions, compute score
   - INTENTS:      GROUP BY intent_sig, count distinct sessions, compute score
   - META-SKILLS:  GROUP BY meta_id, count distinct sessions, compute score
   - CORROBORATED: GROUP BY (intent_sig, gram) ⋈ beats, count sessions, compute score
3. Score formula (per candidate):
   0.25 * min(sessions/30, 1)        ← frequency
   + 0.1 * min(spanDays/120, 1)      ← persistence over time
   + 0.1 * recencyBoost(≤30d: 1.0, ≤90d: 0.6, else: 0.3)
   + 0.15 * regularity               ← longer command sequences
   + 0.15 * specificity              ← fraction NOT in COMMON
   + 0.25 * outcomeRate              ← ok/done; 0.5 when no labeled outcomes
4. Rank by score, filter by --min-sessions
5. Emit wrapped in `<!-- EVIDENCE FOR SYNTHESIS -->` markers
   Each evidence line: `path:line [outcome] intent="…" cmds="…"`
6. stdout: markdown evidence block (agent-readable, not user-facing)
```

#### **`beats --corr "<intent_sig> × <gram>" | --gram | --sig | --meta | --theme | --keys | sampling`**
```
1. selectBeats(db, sel) → rows matching the selector
2. exportRows(db, rows):
   a. stratify(rows, max): sort by outcome (corrected first, success, recent neutral)
   b. for each row:
      - readFileSync(path) → lines
      - start_line ← current beat's start_line
      - end_line ← min(next beat's start_line - 1, capped by --span-lines)
      - span = lines.slice(start_line - 1, end_line).join('\n')
      - redactSecrets(span) → replace secrets with [REDACTED:type]
      - emit: {key: "session_id#ord", ref: "path:line", outcome, toolMix, text}
   c. beatsFingerprint(rows) → SHA-256 of sorted (session_id|ord|start_line|outcome|n_cmds)
3. stdout: JSON {cluster, exported, fingerprint, beats:[...], totalMatching}
   Each beat carries a stable key for cache lookup and deep-mine input
```

#### **`dossier get --key K` / `put --key K --fingerprint F --file <json>`**
```
get:  SELECT json FROM dossiers WHERE cluster_key = ? → stdout
put:  INSERT/REPLACE INTO dossiers(cluster_key, fingerprint, json, created) VALUES(...)
      → "cached dossier for <key>"
render: SELECT json FROM dossiers ORDER BY created DESC
        → stdout: markdown blocks (LAW 1 sentinel appended)
```

#### **`plan render --file <manifest.json>`**
```
1. JSON.parse(manifest)  → {project?, scope?, proposed:[{cluster|theme, name?}], skipped:[...]}
2. for each proposed:
   - getDossier(db, cluster) if cached, else renderThemes(db, theme_id)
   - emit markdown card (### name, evidence, trigger, etc.)
3. for each skipped:
   - emit skip reason
4. Append LAW 1 sentinel: "=== dossiers above: N ==="
5. savePlan(db, manifest) → INSERT INTO plans(manifest) for recall via `plan last`
6. stdout: full plan markdown (the agent presents this verbatim via ExitPlanMode)
```

#### **`forged add --name N --path P --cluster K`**
```
1. inferKind(db, K) → kind (corr | gram | sig | meta | theme)
2. clusterState(db, kind, K) → {fingerprint, sessions, ok, bad}
3. sha(path) → SHA-256 of SKILL.md
4. INSERT INTO forged(name, status, skill_path, cluster_key, kind, fingerprint, sessions, ok, bad, content_sha, created)
5. addRun(db, 'forge', name, summary)
6. stdout: "registered <name> ← <cluster> (fp <hash>, <sessions> sessions, <ok>✓/<bad>✗)"
```

#### **`forged check [--emit json]`**
```
1. SELECT * FROM forged WHERE status='active'
2. for each:
   a. clusterState(db, kind, cluster) → current stats
   b. compare to forge-time stats:
      - fingerprint unchanged → "up-to-date"
      - new corrected beats → "update: N new corrected, sessions X→Y"
      - file hand-edited (content_sha changed) → "update-carefully"
      - file deleted → "orphaned"
      - user declined + evidence unchanged → "suppress"
      - user declined + evidence grew → "re-engage"
3. emit JSON array of {name, recommendation, current_fingerprint, ...}
```

## 5. Output: Files, Format, and SKILL.md Contract

### Corpus Artifacts
```
~/.specstory/lore.db
├─ sessions(id, project_id, project_name, path, date, agent, size, beats, mtime, parser, author, uuid)
├─ beats(id, session_id, ord, start_line, intent_raw, intent_sig, n_tools, tool_mix, files, n_cmds, exit_fails, outcome)
├─ commands(beat_id, ord, head, raw, line)
├─ grams(beat_id, n, gram)
├─ meta_hits(beat_id, meta_id, quote, line)
├─ dossiers(cluster_key, fingerprint, json, created)       ← Phase C cache
├─ themes(theme_id, title, description, beat_keys, fingerprint, evidence, created)
├─ forged(name, status, skill_path, cluster_key, kind, fingerprint, sessions, ok, bad, content_sha, created, note)
├─ runs(id, ts, cmd, scope, summary)                       ← activity journal
└─ plans(id, manifest, created)                            ← saved curation plans
```

### Forged Skill Files
```
~/.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md       ← canonical (write once)
  ├─ frontmatter (agentskills.io format)
  ├─ Steps (from evidence, grounded in real beats)
  ├─ Verification (how the user confirmed it worked)
  ├─ Failure modes (from corrected beats - what went wrong + how to avoid)
  └─ Notes (metadata: "Forged by Lore from N sessions in path (date range), X✓/Y✗ outcomes")

~/.claude/skills/<name> → symlink to ~/.agents/skills/<name>
~/.codex/skills/<name> → symlink to ~/.agents/skills/<name>
(fan-out: write once, symlink everywhere)
```

### SKILL.md Agent Contract

The skill's frontmatter (YAML):
```yaml
---
name: lore
description: SpecStory Lore - mine your SpecStory coding histories...
argument-hint: "Enter = guided setup · or plain English, e.g. 'last 30 days, just show candidates'"
allowed-tools: Bash, Read, Write, AskUserQuestion
license: Apache-2.0
hooks:
  PreToolUse:
    - matcher: "ExitPlanMode"
      hooks:
        - type: command
          command: "node \"${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/hooks/validate-plan.mjs\""
---
```

**The hook:** `scripts/hooks/validate-plan.mjs` is a PreToolUse enforcer that **denies any ExitPlanMode call whose plan body does not contain**:
1. The marker `<!-- PASS-THROUGH FORGE PLAN`
2. The sentinel `=== dossiers above: N ===` as the final line
3. At least N `### ` dossier card headers matching the sentinel count

This enforces **LAW 1** (failure mode #3): no summarizing away the evidence.

### Three LAWs (Output Contract, in SKILL.md)

**LAW 1 - DOSSIERS BEFORE QUESTIONS:**
Every candidate decision must be preceded by a message showing full dossiers for every candidate, ending with the sentinel `=== dossiers above: N ===`.

**LAW 2 - PASS-THROUGH RENDERING:**
The agent must emit the engine's visuals verbatim (not summarized): the badge line, dossier cards, theme cards, plan, with every PASS-THROUGH block intact.

**LAW 3 - NARRATE PHASES:**
Before every long-running call, emit a status line (e.g., `📜 indexing BearClaude (253 sessions)…`) so the window always shows what's happening.

## 6. Conventions

### Language & Runtime
- **Node.js ESM** (`.mjs` files)
- **Minimum version:** Node >= 22.5 (for `node:sqlite`)
- **Zero npm dependencies** (only `node:fs`, `node:crypto`, `node:sqlite`, `node:path`, `node:os`)
- **Parallel tools:** if a change needs an npm package, stop and ask first

### File Layout
```
lore/
├── SKILL.md                          ← agent contract (frontmatter + narrative)
├── HOW-IT-WORKS.md                   ← narrative walkthrough (stage by stage)
├── AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md          ← technical reference (this doc)
├── AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md             ← rules for devs working ON lore
├── CONTRIBUTING.md / README.md
├── package.json                      ← {"type": "module", "engines": {"node": ">=22.5"}}
├── .claude-plugin/plugin.json        ← harness metadata
├── scripts/
│   ├── mine-skills.mjs               ← CLI entry (thin dispatcher)
│   ├── deep-mine.workflow.js         ← Claude Code: Workflow script for Phase C (miner + verifier)
│   ├── theme-sweep.workflow.js       ← Claude Code: Workflow script for Phase 2b′ (thematic lenses)
│   ├── hooks/
│   │   └── validate-plan.mjs         ← PreToolUse hook: LAW 1 enforcement
│   └── lib/
│       ├── patterns.mjs              ← format grammar + classifiers
│       ├── parse.mjs                 ← pure transcript parsing (no I/O)
│       ├── discover.mjs              ← file discovery + stable project ID
│       ├── db.mjs                    ← SQLite schema + migrations
│       ├── indexer.mjs               ← incremental indexing
│       ├── report.mjs                ← corroboration queries + scoring
│       ├── beats.mjs                 ← span export, sampling, dossier cache
│       └── forged.mjs                ← registry (provenance + drift)
├── fixtures/                         ← synthetic transcripts per provider form factor
│   ├── projA/.specstory/history/     ← Claude Code modern + legacy formats
│   ├── projB/.specstory/history/     ← Codex formats
│   ├── projC/.specstory/history/     ← Cursor + semantic channel (themes)
│   ├── provider-*/.specstory/history/← provider-specific format coverage
│   └── golden/forge-plan.md          ← golden file (executable spec)
└── tests/
    └── engine.test.mjs               ← 29+ node:test cases (npm test)
```

### Naming Conventions
- **command heads** - lowercase, hyphenated: `git status`, `go build`, `./scripts/run.sh`
- **intent signatures** - `verb:keyword`: `build:run`, `write:commit`, `fix:divergence`
- **cluster keys** - format-specific:
  - gram: `"git status ▸ git add ▸ git commit"` (n-grams joined with ▸)
  - intent: `"write:commit"` (intent_sig)
  - corr: `"write:commit × git status ▸ git add ▸ git commit"` (intent_sig × gram)
  - meta: detector id like `"read-only-diagnosis"`
  - theme: `"freeze-first"` or `"theme:freeze-first"` (stable theme id)
- **session ids** - `project_id/filename` (e.g., `stoa/2026-05-01_10-00-00Z-can-we-run-a.md`)
- **beat keys** - `session_id#ord` (stable across re-indexing, survives file moves)

### Linting & Formatting
- **No em dashes** anywhere (docs, comments, engine output) - use " - " instead
- **Conventional commits** with a why-body: `type(scope): subject`
- **Fixtures are the spec** - new parsing claims need fixture coverage
- **PARSER_VERSION** bump when behavior changes (auto re-parse on next `index`)

### Testing
```bash
npm test                    # 29+ cases via node:test (no test framework deps)
UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 npm test   # regenerate fixtures/golden/forge-plan.md if layout changes
```

Test command in package.json:
```json
"scripts": {
  "test": "node --test tests/*.test.mjs"
}
```

**Test structure** (`tests/engine.test.mjs`):
- **Unit tests** - pure `parse.mjs` functions (`headsFrom`, `extractShellBlock`, `parseSessionFile`, `intentSig`)
- **Integration tests** - index fixtures → assert multi-agent tags, corroborated pairs, cross-project portability
- **Idempotency tests** - index twice (second skipped), `--force` (replace, not duplicate), `prune` (no orphans)
- **Phase C tests** - stratified export, fingerprint stability, dossier cache roundtrip

---

## 7. How the Skill is Wired

### Plugin Metadata (`.claude-plugin/plugin.json`)
```json
{
  "name": "lore",
  "displayName": "SpecStory Lore",
  "version": "3.9.0",
  "description": "Mine your SpecStory coding histories...",
  "author": {"name": "SpecStory", "url": "https://github.com/specstoryai"},
  "homepage": "https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/tree/dev/lore",
  "repository": "https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory",
  "license": "Apache-2.0",
  "keywords": ["skills", "specstory", "mining", "agent-skills", ...]
}
```

### User Invocation → Execution Flow

**In Claude Code:**
```
/lore [args]
  ↓
Claude Code framework discovers skill at ~/.agents/skills/lore or ~/.claude/skills/lore
  ↓
SKILL.md frontmatter parsed:
  - name: lore
  - allowed-tools: Bash, Read, Write, AskUserQuestion
  - hooks: PreToolUse on ExitPlanMode → validate-plan.mjs
  ↓
Agent executes SKILL.md narrative (Steps 0–6):
  Step 0.25: if no args, ask(Scope / Window / Goal)
  Step 0.5:  interpret args → engine flags
  Step 1:    Bash: node scripts/mine-skills.mjs index --dir ...
             Bash: node scripts/mine-skills.mjs report ...
  Step 2:    agent synthesizes candidates from evidence
  Step 2b:   agent verifies each candidate (opens refs, reads spans)
  Step 2b′:  theme sweep (agent spawns subagents for 6 thematic lenses)
  Step 2c:   deep-mine (Workflow + subagents, or sequential)
  Step 3:    enter plan mode, present curation via ExitPlanMode
             PreToolUse hook: DENY if plan ≠ engine-rendered artifact
  Step 4:    on approval, forge each skill (Write files to ~/.agents/skills/<name>)
             Register via: Bash: node scripts/mine-skills.mjs forged add ...
  Step 5:    privacy scrub (no secrets in SKILL.md)
  Step 6:    report what was forged
             Bash: node scripts/mine-skills.mjs runs add --summary "..."
```

**In other harnesses (Codex, Cursor, Gemini):**
- Skill auto-discovered from `~/.agents/skills/lore` or harness-specific dir
- No ExitPlanMode or plan mode → fallback path:
  - Agent emits dossier message with sentinel
  - Ask via numbered list (not single-select)
  - LAW 1 check: prior message ends with `=== dossiers above: N ===`
  - Same SKILL.md narrative, degrades gracefully

### Repository Install (Live Clone)
```bash
# Canonical
~/.agents/skills/lore → symlink to ~/getspecstory/lore

# Fan-out per harness
~/.claude/skills/lore → symlink to ~/.agents/skills/lore
~/.codex/skills/lore → symlink to ~/.agents/skills/lore

# A git pull in ~/getspecstory updates every harness instantly (symlinks, no copies)
```

## 8. Exact npm / Test Commands

From **package.json**:
```bash
npm test              # runs: node --test tests/*.test.mjs
```

**Common development commands** (not in package.json but in CLAUDE.md):
```bash
# Development corpus (never write to ~/.specstory/lore.db)
node scripts/mine-skills.mjs index --dir fixtures/projA/.specstory/history --db /tmp/dev-lore.db
node scripts/mine-skills.mjs report --db /tmp/dev-lore.db
node scripts/mine-skills.mjs beats --gram "go build ▸ go test" --db /tmp/dev-lore.db

# Regenerate golden file
UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 npm test

# No external test runners, no package deps - pure node:test
```

---

## Summary: Why This Architecture for /workthreads

The /lore pattern is optimal for /workthreads because:

1. **Deterministic beats** - a universal model for mining ANY agent interaction (text spans + outcome labels)
2. **Local-only engine** - parses once, caches patterns in SQLite, the agent only reads digested evidence
3. **Incremental + idempotent** - fingerprints ensure re-runs are cheap and safe
4. **Registry memory** - forged skills are tracked, drift-detected, updated (never duplicated)
5. **Multi-agent support** - one parser works for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini, etc. (provider headers match generically)
6. **Harness-portable** - the skill degrades gracefully from plan mode (Claude Code) to sentinel-proven fallback (everywhere else)

**Mirror this pattern for /workthreads:** same module structure, same beats model, same registry discipline, same "evidence export → agent judges" boundary. Replace "coding histories" with "work threads" (Slack, GitHub, Asana, whatever) and the architecture stays the same.
