7	export function wantedKinds(kinds) {
8	  if (!kinds || !kinds.length) return new Set(['cmd', 'task', 'meta', 'corr'])
9	  const out = new Set()
10	  for (const k of kinds) {
11	    if (['cmd', 'command', 'commands', 'runbook-cmd'].includes(k)) out.add('cmd')
12	    else if (['task', 'tasks', 'intent', 'intents', 'runbook-task'].includes(k)) out.add('task')
13	    else if (['meta', 'meta-skill', 'metaskill', 'meta-skills'].includes(k)) out.add('meta')
14	    else if (['corr', 'corroborated', 'deep'].includes(k)) out.add('corr')
15	    else if (['runbook', 'runbooks'].includes(k)) { out.add('cmd'); out.add('task'); out.add('corr') }
16	  }
17	  return out.size ? out : new Set(['cmd', 'task', 'meta', 'corr'])
18	}
19	
20	function recencyBoost(last, maxDate) {
21	  if (!last || !maxDate) return 0.5
22	  const d = (Date.parse(maxDate) - Date.parse(last)) / 864e5
23	  return d <= 30 ? 1 : d <= 90 ? 0.6 : 0.3
24	}
25	function specificityOf(key) {
26	  const heads = key.split(' ▸ ')
27	  const non = heads.filter(h => !COMMON.has(h.split(' ')[0])).length
28	  return heads.length ? non / heads.length : 0.5
29	}
30	
31	export function report(db, args, write = (s) => process.stdout.write(s)) {

33	  const dayFilter = args.days > 0 ? `AND s.date >= '${new Date(Date.now() - args.days * 864e5).toISOString().slice(0, 10)}'` : ''
34	  const like = args.filter ? args.filter.replace(/'/g, "''") : ''
35

37	  if (!scope.c) {
38	    write('📜 lore · the corpus is empty - index something first: mine-skills.mjs index --scan <project>\n')
39	    return { scope: { sessions: 0, projects: 0 }, runbooks: [], intents: [], metas: [], corroborated: [] }
40	  }
41	  const maxDate = scope.d1
42	  const projNames = Object.fromEntries(db.prepare('SELECT DISTINCT project_id, project_name FROM sessions').all().map(r => [r.project_id, r.project_name]))
43	  const crossProject = scope.p > 1

45	  function score(r, reg, spec) {
46	    return +(0.25 * Math.min(r.sess / 30, 1) + 0.1 * Math.min(((Date.parse(r.last) - Date.parse(r.first)) / 864e5 || 0) / 120, 1)
47	      + 0.1 * recencyBoost(r.last, maxDate) + 0.15 * reg + 0.15 * spec
48	      + 0.25 * (r.done > 0 ? r.ok / r.done : 0.5)).toFixed(3)   // outcome success-rate is a first-class term
49	  }

62	             MIN(e.id) sample_ep

1	<h1 align="center">📜 Lore</h1>
2	
3	<p align="center"><strong>Your sessions are your lore. Forge them into skills.</strong></p>
4	
5	<p align="center">
6	  <a href="https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/actions/workflows/lore-validate.yml"><img src="https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/actions/workflows/lore-validate.yml/badge.svg" alt="Lore Validate"></a>

9	  <img src="https://img.shields.io/badge/dependencies-0-brightgreen" alt="Zero dependencies">
10	</p>
11	
12	<p align="center">
13	Lore mines the SpecStory histories your coding agents leave behind  - <br>
14	finds the workflows you actually repeat, proves them with evidence and outcomes,<br>
15	and forges the ones you choose into skills installed across every agent you use.
16	</p>
17	
18	
19	
20	https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/082b51e7-2283-4204-a093-45b8b1ce3ce1
21	
22	
23	
24	---
25	
26	## Install
27	
28	```zsh
29	npx skills add specstoryai/getspecstory --skill lore
30	```
31	
32	That detects every supported agent on your machine (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, and
33	more) and installs lore into each. Requires Node ≥ 22.5.
34	
35	Installs are copies, so they don't change until you update them:
36	
37	```zsh
38	npx skills update lore    # or `npx skills update` to refresh every installed skill
39	```
40	
41	Alternatively, in Claude Code, install it as a plugin:
42	
43	```
44	/plugin marketplace add specstoryai/getspecstory
45	/plugin install lore@specstory
46	```
47	
48	Plugin installs update via `/plugin update lore`.
49	
50	## Get started
51	
52	In any agent that reads [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, …):
53	
54	```
55	/lore
56	```
57	
58	(Invocation differs per harness - see
59	[Optimized for Claude Code, built for every harness](#optimized-for-claude-code-built-for-every-harness).)
60	
61	Press Enter and it walks you through scope, time window, and goal - then mines, shows you
62	evidence-backed dossiers of your candidate skills, and presents a forge plan to approve. Or steer it
63	in plain English - there is no argument grammar to learn:
64	
65	| Say | Get |
66	|---|---|
67	| *(just Enter)* | Guided setup, then the full pipeline. |
68	| `mine this project` | Mine this repo's history. |
69	| `across my projects in ~/code` | Cross-project mining: portable vs project-specific skills. |
70	| `last 30 days, just show candidates` | Dry run: evidence dossiers only, no forging. |
71	| `about supabase` / `only my judgment skills` | Narrow by topic, or by channel (themes vs runbooks). |
72	| `status` | What Lore has done: corpus, themes, forged skills, drift. |
73	| `what skills do I have?` | Inventory of every installed skill and what it does. |
74	| `show me the last plan` | Recall a canceled forge plan and resume. |
75	| `forge them all` | Batch forge after one confirmation. |
76	| `reset my lore` | Start fresh (asks first; forged skills stay installed). |
77	
78	Everything accumulates in one file - `~/.specstory/lore.db` - incrementally and idempotently, across
79	all your projects and agents. Prefer the engine directly? It's one zero-dependency script - see
80	[Using the engine directly](HOW-IT-WORKS.md#using-the-engine-directly).
81	
82	## What it finds
83	
84	Lore's unit is the **beat**: your prompt (the intent), everything the agent did until your next
85	prompt (the method - real executed commands, files, exit codes), and your reply as a free outcome
86	label (approval ✓ or correction ✗). Patterns that recur across beats, sessions, projects, and
87	**teammates** become candidates; the strongest are **corroborated** - you asked for X and the agent
88	did Y, repeatedly, and it worked. And beyond commands, **theme mining** reads the conversational
89	beats - the reviews, decisions, and corrections - and surfaces the *latent* expertise you operate
90	without naming: how you review, how you diagnose, how you direct a model.
91	
92	```
93	📜 Lore mined!
94	├─ 🗂  projects: stoa 1,243 · BearClaude 253
95	├─ 🧠 beats: 21,346 · ⚙️ executed commands: 36,474
96	├─ 🤖 agents: claude-code 1,375 · codex-cli 310 · cursor 6
97	├─ 👥 authors: Greg 1,243 · Sean 181 · Jake 72
98	├─ 🎯 outcomes: 744 ✓ approvals · 693 ✗ corrections
99	└─ 📦 your lore: ~/.specstory/lore.db
100	```
101	
102	## Why it's different
103	
104	- **Deterministic engine, judging agent.** A zero-dependency parser + SQLite engine does the
105	  counting; your agent does the naming and judging. The engine can't hallucinate, and the agent
106	  never reads 400k-line transcripts - only engine-exported evidence, with credential values
107	  mechanically redacted before the model ever sees them.
108	- **Outcomes from your own replies.** "No, wait - " marks a failure; "perfect, commit it" marks
109	  success. Skills are ranked by what actually worked, not what merely happened.
110	- **Latent expertise, not just runbooks.** Thematic lenses mine your judgment work - review craft,
111	  decision-making, model direction - into skills you didn't know you had ("huh, I *do* do that").
112	  Verified themes then **expand from anecdote to measurement**: the engine finds every corpus
113	  occurrence deterministically and reports the practice's **outcome lift** over your baseline.
114	- **Deep-mine with an adversary.** Top candidates get one subagent reading *every* beat
115	  (failures first) and a second trying to refute the result. Failure modes with recoveries are what
116	  make a forged skill deep instead of a runbook.
117	- **Team-aware.** Histories committed by teammates are attributed (git author → home-dir →
118	  machine user); a workflow several people share is a team skill, proposed for the repo - and never
119	  presented as yours when it isn't.
120	- **Forge once, install everywhere.** Skills land in `~/.agents/skills/<name>` and symlink into
121	  every harness. The registry remembers what was forged and declined, and proposes **updates** when
122	  the evidence grows - re-runs never duplicate.
123	
124	<p align="center"><sub>Reads histories from every SpecStory provider: Claude Code · Codex · Cursor · Gemini · Factory Droid · DeepSeek · Antigravity - modern and legacy formats alike.</sub></p>
125	
126	## Optimized for Claude Code, built for every harness
127	
128	Lore is tuned for Claude Code: the two heavy phases ship as bundled **Workflow scripts** that fan
129	out subagents in parallel - deep mining runs one miner plus one adversarial verifier per candidate
130	cluster, theme sweeping runs one miner per thematic lens - and runs are resumable if interrupted.
131	Setup is a guided three-question start, and curation is presented as a **plan you approve** before
132	anything is written. The plan itself is engine-assembled and **hook-enforced**: a `PreToolUse` hook
133	bundled with the skill rejects any curation plan that does not embed the full evidence verbatim, so
134	you can never approve a forge you have not seen.
135	
136	The skill is still harness-portable by design. The deterministic core (the parser, the corpus, the
137	registry) is a zero-dependency Node script that behaves identically everywhere, and the skill
138	contract degrades gracefully: harnesses with their own subagent mechanism fan out the same miner
139	and verifier briefs; harnesses without subagents mine the clusters sequentially with the agent
140	reading the engine's evidence exports directly. Forged skills are plain markdown either way, usable
141	from any agent.
142	
143	After [installing](#install), invoke it per harness:
144	
145	| Harness | Invocation |
146	|---|---|
147	| Claude Code | `/lore` |
148	| Codex | `$lore` (the `/` prefix is reserved for built-ins; also listed under `/skills`) |
149	| Cursor | skills load automatically - just ask, e.g. "mine my lore" |
150	| Gemini CLI | reads `~/.agents/skills` natively - just ask; the model activates the skill (with your consent) |
151	
152	## Developing
153	
154	Lore lives in the [getspecstory](https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory) monorepo, next to
155	the SpecStory CLI. For development, install from a clone - every install point is a symlink back
156	to it, so updating is just `git -C ~/getspecstory pull`:
157	
158	```zsh
159	# 1. clone the monorepo anywhere you keep code
160	git clone git@github.com:specstoryai/getspecstory.git ~/getspecstory
161	
162	# 2. canonical skill location (Codex and Gemini CLI read ~/.agents/skills natively)
163	mkdir -p ~/.agents/skills && ln -sfn ~/getspecstory/lore ~/.agents/skills/lore
164	
165	# 3. fan out into every harness skills dir you have (symlink, never copy)
166	for h in ~/.claude/skills ~/.codex/skills; do
167	  [ -d "$h" ] && ln -sfn ~/.agents/skills/lore "$h/lore"
168	done
169	```

1	// forged.mjs - the forged-skill registry: Lore's memory of what it has already surfaced and built.
2	//
3	// Three jobs, all deterministic:
4	// 1. PROVENANCE - when a skill is forged, record which cluster it came from and the evidence
5	//    state at forge time (fingerprint, session count, outcome rates, content hash of the file).
6	// 2. DECISIONS - when the user declines a candidate, record that too, so later runs do not
7	//    re-propose it unless the evidence has grown materially.
8	// 3. DRIFT - `check` recomputes each cluster's current state and reports what changed since
9	//    forge time: new beats, new corrected beats (fresh failure-mode material), outcome
10	//    shifts, and whether the installed file was hand-edited or deleted. The calling agent turns
11	//    drift into "propose an update to skill X", never a duplicate.
12	
13	import { readFileSync, existsSync } from 'node:fs'
14	import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
15	import { selectBeats, beatsFingerprint, getTheme } from './beats.mjs'
16	import { META } from './patterns.mjs'
17	
18	export function ensureForgedTable(db) {
19	  db.exec(`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS forged(
20	    name TEXT PRIMARY KEY,            -- skill name (or 'declined:<cluster>' for declines)
21	    status TEXT,                      -- active | declined
22	    skill_path TEXT,                  -- where the SKILL.md was written ('' for declines)
23	    cluster_key TEXT, kind TEXT,      -- kind: corr | gram | sig | meta | theme
24	    fingerprint TEXT,                 -- beatsFingerprint at forge/decline time
25	    sessions INTEGER, ok INTEGER, bad INTEGER,   -- evidence stats at forge/decline time
26	    content_sha TEXT,                 -- sha256 of the written SKILL.md (hand-edit detection)
27	    created TEXT, note TEXT)`)
28	}
29	
30	// Infer the cluster kind from its shape when the caller does not say. Order matters:
31	//   "theme:<id>" or a saved theme id -> theme     "intent × gram" -> corr     "a ▸ b" -> gram
32	//   a META detector id -> meta                    otherwise -> sig ("write:commit")
33	export function inferKind(db, key) {
34	  if (key.startsWith('theme:')) return 'theme'
35	  if (key.includes(' × ')) return 'corr'
36	  if (key.includes(' ▸ ')) return 'gram'
37	  try { if (getTheme(db, key)) return 'theme' } catch { /* no themes table yet */ }
38	  if (META.some(m => m.id === key)) return 'meta'
39	  return 'sig'
40	}
41	
42	// Evidence stats for a cluster of ANY kind (selectBeats resolves themes too). A stats lookup must
43	// never lose a registry write: on any failure this degrades to zeros instead of throwing.
44	function clusterState(db, kind, key) {
45	  try {
46	    const rows = selectBeats(db, { [kind]: key })
47	    const sess = new Set(rows.map(r => r.session_id)).size
48	    const ok = rows.filter(r => r.outcome === 'success').length
49	    const bad = rows.filter(r => r.outcome === 'corrected').length
50	    return { fingerprint: beatsFingerprint(rows), beats: rows.length, sessions: sess, ok, bad }
51	  } catch (err) {
52	    process.stderr.write(`forged: stats lookup failed for ${kind}:"${key}" (${err.message}) - recording with empty stats\n`)
53	    return { fingerprint: '', beats: 0, sessions: 0, ok: 0, bad: 0 }
54	  }
55	}
56	
57	function sha(path) {
58	  try { return createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(path)).digest('hex').slice(0, 16) } catch { return '' }
59	}
60	
61	export function addForged(db, { name, path, cluster, kind, note = '' }) {
62	  ensureForgedTable(db)
63	  kind = kind || inferKind(db, cluster)
64	  const st = clusterState(db, kind, cluster)
65	  db.prepare(`INSERT OR REPLACE INTO forged(name,status,skill_path,cluster_key,kind,fingerprint,sessions,ok,bad,content_sha,created,note)
66	              VALUES(?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?)`)
67	    .run(name, 'active', path, cluster, kind, st.fingerprint, st.sessions, st.ok, st.bad, sha(path), new Date().toISOString(), note)
68	  return st
69	}
70	
71	export function declineCandidate(db, { cluster, kind, note = '' }) {
72	  ensureForgedTable(db)
73	  kind = kind || inferKind(db, cluster)
74	  const st = clusterState(db, kind, cluster)
75	  db.prepare(`INSERT OR REPLACE INTO forged(name,status,skill_path,cluster_key,kind,fingerprint,sessions,ok,bad,content_sha,created,note)
76	              VALUES(?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?)`)
77	    .run('declined:' + cluster, 'declined', '', cluster, kind, st.fingerprint, st.sessions, st.ok, st.bad, '', new Date().toISOString(), note)
78	  return st
79	}
80

37	  const SKIP = new Set(['node_modules', 'build', 'dist', 'out', 'target', 'vendor', 'Pods', 'DerivedData'])
38	  const found = []
39	  const walk = (dir, depth) => {
40	    if (depth > maxDepth) return

42	    try { ents = readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true }) } catch { return }
43	    for (const e of ents) {

45	      if (e.name === '.specstory') {

47	        if (existsSync(hd)) found.push(hd)

52	    }
53	  }

# Lore Skill Architecture - Complete Technical Summary

## Executive Summary: The Pattern

**Lore is a deterministic engine + agent synthesis system.** The engine parses transcripts into beats (intent → method → outcome), counts and caches patterns in SQLite, and exports evidence. The agent reads only that evidence, names/judges/deep-mines, and forges skills. **You can never hallucinate in the engine; the agent never reads whole transcripts.**

---

## 1. Deterministic Beats Architecture

### What are "Beats"?
A **beat** is the atomic unit of analysis:
- **INTENT** - one user turn / prompt (≤30 lines, text only)
- **METHOD** - everything the agent does until the next user turn: executed commands, files touched, tool types used, exit-code failures
- **OUTCOME** - labeled retroactively from the user's next turn (via regex classifiers):
  - `✓ success` - "ok", "perfect", approval language
  - `✗ corrected` - "no wait", "still wrong", steering corrections
  - `· neutral` - new task (most beats)
  - `end` - session closes

**The outcome trick:** Your own next reply is free supervision. No annotations needed.

### The Deterministic Pipeline (5 Phases)

```
Phase 1: PARSE BEATS (deterministic, zero LLM)
  .specstory/history/*.md  →  text walk  →  beat rows (no I/O during parse)
  ├─ extract intent (USER marker → intent_raw, intent_sig via verb+keyword)
  ├─ extract method (shell/read/write tools, commands, files, exit codes)
  ├─ accumulate into beats
  └─ retroactively label outcomes (beat[k].outcome = classifyOutcome(beat[k+1].opening))

Phase 2: INDEX (incremental, idempotent)
  parse → INSERT/REPLACE into corpus  (~/.specstory/lore.db)
  ├─ fingerprint = size + mtime + PARSER_VERSION (unchanged files skipped)
  ├─ session id = project_id + '/' + filename (stable across reorganizations)
  └─ author attributed: git add-author → path sniff → machine user

Phase 2d: FOUR CANDIDATE CHANNELS (SQL GROUP BYs)
  beats  ├─  COMMANDS (n-grams over executed cmds, grouped by gram)
         ├─  INTENTS (verb:keyword signatures, grouped by intent_sig)
         ├─  META (way-of-working detectors - read-only-diagnosis, reasoning-dial, etc.)
         └─  THEMES (semantic clusters - LLM lenses over conversational beats)

Phase 2b: CORROBORATION (strongest truth signal)
  Intent × Procedure co-occurring in SAME beats:
  "the user asked for X and the agent did Y, repeatedly" - reported with outcome rates
  SQL: beats ⋈ grams WHERE intent_sig = ? AND gram = ?

Phase 3: DEEP-MINE (per harness, cached)
  cluster → beats export (stratified: corrected first, success, recent neutral)
            → content fingerprint (from session_id, ord, start_line, outcome, n_cmds)
            → one MINER reads every beat + one ADVERSARIAL VERIFIER
            → dossier cache (keyed by cluster_key + fingerprint)
            → verified dossier replaces sampled version
```

**The state machine is implicit in the code flow, not explicit.** Each phase is triggered by the agent's control - there is no loop or state enum. The "beats" are materialized in `scripts/lib/beats.mjs` and cached in the `dossiers` SQLite table.

---

## 2. Local-Only vs Cloud/Online

**There is no "local-only" mode distinct from a cloud mode.** Lore runs entirely local:
- All parsing and counting happens in `scripts/lib/*.mjs` (Node.js, zero network, zero API keys)
- Corpus stored at `~/.specstory/lore.db` (one SQLite file, portable)
- No cloud backend, no external services
- The only network call is when the agent optionally spawns subagents (deep-mine / theme mining), which are HARNESS-SPECIFIC:
  - **Claude Code:** runs `scripts/deep-mine.workflow.js` (bundled Workflow script, parallel subagents via Claude Code's Workflow mechanism)
  - **Codex / others:** spawn their own parallel subagents with the same briefs
  - **Sequential fallback:** agent reads `beats` export and mines linearly (no subagents)

**What "local-only" likely means in your user's comment:** The Lore engine has **zero external dependencies** and zero hallucination vectors - it's pure parsing + SQL. That's why it's deterministic.

---

## 3. Input: Reading SpecStory Histories

### Paths and Formats
```
.specstory/history/*.md          ← default (current project)
.specstory/history/202X-*/…      ← nested by year/month (specstory-organize layout)
~/code/*//.specstory/history/    ← cross-project mode (--projects ~/code)
(any depth)                       ← --scan . finds all at any depth (monorepos)
```

### Parsing Libraries
- **Entry:** `scripts/lib/discover.mjs`
  - `walkMd(dir)` - recursively list *.md files (handles year/month nesting)
  - `readLabel(historyDir)` - stable project identity from `.specstory/.project.json` (git_id preferred)
  - `scanForHistories(root, maxDepth=6)` - monorepo discovery (skips node_modules, build, etc.)
  - `discoverProjects(args)` - resolves `--dir`, `--projects`, `--scan` into `{historyDir, id, name}[]`

- **Core:** `scripts/lib/parse.mjs` (pure function, fully unit-testable)
  - `parseSessionFile(text)` → `{agent, uuid, beats: [...]}`
    - Walks transcript once, segments at `_**User**_` markers
    - Extracts intent (≤30 lines), method tools, and outcome labels
  - `extractShellBlock(summary, body, line)` → `{cmds: [{cmd, line}], fails}`
    - Handles **4 command locations** (modern + legacy):
      1. Codex in-summary: `` `cmd` `` inside `<summary>`
      2. Claude single-line: inline-backtick body line
      3. Multi-line: bash/sh/zsh/shell fence (heredoc bodies skipped)
      4. Codex legacy "- command:" bullet (can be multi-line)
  - `headsFrom(cmd)` → `[head1, head2, ...]`
    - Splits chains (`&&`, `;`), strips env prefixes, unwraps `bash -lc`, drops noise
    - Keeps subcommands (`git status`) and project scripts (`./scripts/run.sh`)
  - `intentSig(raw)` → `"verb:keyword"` (e.g. `"build:run"`, `"write:commit"`)
    - Leading verb from `VERBS`, first salient keyword via `tokenize`/`STOP`

### Pattern Grammar
All patterns in `scripts/lib/patterns.mjs`:
```
SESSION_HDR         - <!-- <Provider> Session <uuid> (ts) -->
USER_MARK, TURN_MARK - _**User**_, _**Agent**_
TOOLUSE_OPEN        - <tool-use data-tool-type="T" ...>
SUMMARY_CMD         - backtick in <summary>
INLINE_CMD          - backtick on body line
FENCE_LINE          - ```bash / ```sh / etc.
HEREDOC_OPEN        - <<'EOF' marker (skip content)
BULLET_CMD          - - command: `[...]`
SHELL_TOOLS         - executor names (Bash, exec_command, shell, shell_command)
SHELL_EXCLUDE       - noise (LS, list_directory, TaskOutput, KillShell)
META                - fixed detector patterns (read-only-diagnosis, reasoning-dial, trace-code-paths, ...)
CORRECTED_RE        - "no|wait|still|wrong|..." regex
SUCCESS_RE          - "ok|perfect|great|go ahead|..." regex
VERBS               - ~200 action verbs (build, write, run, fix, check, ...)
STOP                - common noise words (the, a, to, for, ...)
NOISE               - recon commands (cd, nl, grep, sed, head, tail, ...)
COMMON              - universal commands (git, ls, cat, ...)
```

---

## 4. The Engine: Module Breakdown and Control Flow

### Entry Point
**`scripts/mine-skills.mjs`** - thin CLI dispatcher (272 lines)
- Parses `process.argv` into `ARGS` object
- Dispatches to subcommands
- Returns results to `process.stdout` / `process.stderr`

### Core Library Modules

| File | Responsibility | Key Functions |
|------|---|---|
| **patterns.mjs** | Format grammar + classifiers | `SESSION_HDR`, `TOOLUSE_OPEN`, `CORRECTED_RE`/`SUCCESS_RE`, `classifyOutcome()`, `tokenize()`, `redactSecrets()` |
| **parse.mjs** | Pure text → beats | `parseSessionFile()`, `extractShellBlock()`, `headsFrom()`, `intentSig()`, `sniffAuthor()` |
| **discover.mjs** | File discovery + stable project ID | `walkMd()`, `readLabel()`, `scanForHistories()`, `discoverProjects()`, `fileDate()` |
| **db.mjs** | SQLite schema + migrations | `openDb()`, `PARSER_VERSION`, `deleteSessionRows()`, `addRun()`/`listRuns()` |
| **indexer.mjs** | Incremental indexing pipeline | `indexCorpus()`, `pruneCorpus()`, `gitAuthors()` |
| **report.mjs** | Corroboration queries + scoring | `report()`, `status()`, `skillsInventory()`, `wantedKinds()`, scoring formula |
| **beats.mjs** | Span export, sampling, dossier cache | `exportBeats()`, `exportRows()`, `sampleBeats()`, `selectBeats()`, `stratify()`, `beatsFingerprint()`, `getDossier()`/`putDossier()/`renderDossiers()`, `putTheme()`/`listThemes()`/`renderThemes()`, `expandTheme()`/`growTheme()`, `renderForgePlan()` |
| **forged.mjs** | Registry (provenance + drift) | `addForged()`, `declineCandidate()`, `listForged()`, `checkForged()`, `inferKind()` |

### Control Flow by Subcommand

#### **`index --dir <hist> | --projects <parent> | --scan <root>`**
```
1. discover.discoverProjects(args)  → [{historyDir, id, name}...]
2. for each project:
     discover.walkMd(historyDir)    → [path1, path2, ...]
     for each .md file:
       fs.statSync → fingerprint (size + mtime)
       check db: is this (project_id/filename) known + unchanged?
       if no: 
         fs.readFileSync → text
         parse.parseSessionFile(text) → {agent, uuid, beats:[...]}
         db transaction:
           INSERT sessions row
           for each beat:
             INSERT beats row
             for each command head:
               INSERT commands row
               for each n-gram (n=2..4):
                 INSERT grams row
             for each META detector hit:
               INSERT meta_hits row
3. db.addRun('index', projects, summary)
4. stdout: "indexed N sessions (M unchanged) → ~/.specstory/lore.db"
```

#### **`report [--min-sessions N] [--top N] [--days N] [--kind cmd,task,meta,corr] [--filter S]`**
```
1. SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sessions → scope (projects, sessions)
2. For each wanted kind:
   - RUNBOOKS:     GROUP BY gram, count distinct sessions, compute score
   - INTENTS:      GROUP BY intent_sig, count distinct sessions, compute score
   - META-SKILLS:  GROUP BY meta_id, count distinct sessions, compute score
   - CORROBORATED: GROUP BY (intent_sig, gram) ⋈ beats, count sessions, compute score
3. Score formula (per candidate):
   0.25 * min(sessions/30, 1)        ← frequency
   + 0.1 * min(spanDays/120, 1)      ← persistence over time
   + 0.1 * recencyBoost(≤30d: 1.0, ≤90d: 0.6, else: 0.3)
   + 0.15 * regularity               ← longer command sequences
   + 0.15 * specificity              ← fraction NOT in COMMON
   + 0.25 * outcomeRate              ← ok/done; 0.5 when no labeled outcomes
4. Rank by score, filter by --min-sessions
5. Emit wrapped in `<!-- EVIDENCE FOR SYNTHESIS -->` markers
   Each evidence line: `path:line [outcome] intent="…" cmds="…"`
6. stdout: markdown evidence block (agent-readable, not user-facing)
```

#### **`beats --corr "<intent_sig> × <gram>" | --gram | --sig | --meta | --theme | --keys | sampling`**
```
1. selectBeats(db, sel) → rows matching the selector
2. exportRows(db, rows):
   a. stratify(rows, max): sort by outcome (corrected first, success, recent neutral)
   b. for each row:
      - readFileSync(path) → lines
      - start_line ← current beat's start_line
      - end_line ← min(next beat's start_line - 1, capped by --span-lines)
      - span = lines.slice(start_line - 1, end_line).join('\n')
      - redactSecrets(span) → replace secrets with [REDACTED:type]
      - emit: {key: "session_id#ord", ref: "path:line", outcome, toolMix, text}
   c. beatsFingerprint(rows) → SHA-256 of sorted (session_id|ord|start_line|outcome|n_cmds)
3. stdout: JSON {cluster, exported, fingerprint, beats:[...], totalMatching}
   Each beat carries a stable key for cache lookup and deep-mine input
```

#### **`dossier get --key K` / `put --key K --fingerprint F --file <json>`**
```
get:  SELECT json FROM dossiers WHERE cluster_key = ? → stdout
put:  INSERT/REPLACE INTO dossiers(cluster_key, fingerprint, json, created) VALUES(...)
      → "cached dossier for <key>"
render: SELECT json FROM dossiers ORDER BY created DESC
        → stdout: markdown blocks (LAW 1 sentinel appended)
```

#### **`plan render --file <manifest.json>`**
```
1. JSON.parse(manifest)  → {project?, scope?, proposed:[{cluster|theme, name?}], skipped:[...]}
2. for each proposed:
   - getDossier(db, cluster) if cached, else renderThemes(db, theme_id)
   - emit markdown card (### name, evidence, trigger, etc.)
3. for each skipped:
   - emit skip reason
4. Append LAW 1 sentinel: "=== dossiers above: N ==="
5. savePlan(db, manifest) → INSERT INTO plans(manifest) for recall via `plan last`
6. stdout: full plan markdown (the agent presents this verbatim via ExitPlanMode)
```

#### **`forged add --name N --path P --cluster K`**
```
1. inferKind(db, K) → kind (corr | gram | sig | meta | theme)
2. clusterState(db, kind, K) → {fingerprint, sessions, ok, bad}
3. sha(path) → SHA-256 of SKILL.md
4. INSERT INTO forged(name, status, skill_path, cluster_key, kind, fingerprint, sessions, ok, bad, content_sha, created)
5. addRun(db, 'forge', name, summary)
6. stdout: "registered <name> ← <cluster> (fp <hash>, <sessions> sessions, <ok>✓/<bad>✗)"
```

#### **`forged check [--emit json]`**
```
1. SELECT * FROM forged WHERE status='active'
2. for each:
   a. clusterState(db, kind, cluster) → current stats
   b. compare to forge-time stats:
      - fingerprint unchanged → "up-to-date"
      - new corrected beats → "update: N new corrected, sessions X→Y"
      - file hand-edited (content_sha changed) → "update-carefully"
      - file deleted → "orphaned"
      - user declined + evidence unchanged → "suppress"
      - user declined + evidence grew → "re-engage"
3. emit JSON array of {name, recommendation, current_fingerprint, ...}
```

## 5. Output: Files, Format, and SKILL.md Contract

### Corpus Artifacts
```
~/.specstory/lore.db
├─ sessions(id, project_id, project_name, path, date, agent, size, beats, mtime, parser, author, uuid)
├─ beats(id, session_id, ord, start_line, intent_raw, intent_sig, n_tools, tool_mix, files, n_cmds, exit_fails, outcome)
├─ commands(beat_id, ord, head, raw, line)
├─ grams(beat_id, n, gram)
├─ meta_hits(beat_id, meta_id, quote, line)
├─ dossiers(cluster_key, fingerprint, json, created)       ← Phase C cache
├─ themes(theme_id, title, description, beat_keys, fingerprint, evidence, created)
├─ forged(name, status, skill_path, cluster_key, kind, fingerprint, sessions, ok, bad, content_sha, created, note)
├─ runs(id, ts, cmd, scope, summary)                       ← activity journal
└─ plans(id, manifest, created)                            ← saved curation plans
```

### Forged Skill Files
```
~/.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md       ← canonical (write once)
  ├─ frontmatter (agentskills.io format)
  ├─ Steps (from evidence, grounded in real beats)
  ├─ Verification (how the user confirmed it worked)
  ├─ Failure modes (from corrected beats - what went wrong + how to avoid)
  └─ Notes (metadata: "Forged by Lore from N sessions in path (date range), X✓/Y✗ outcomes")

~/.claude/skills/<name> → symlink to ~/.agents/skills/<name>
~/.codex/skills/<name> → symlink to ~/.agents/skills/<name>
(fan-out: write once, symlink everywhere)
```

### SKILL.md Agent Contract

The skill's frontmatter (YAML):
```yaml
---
name: lore
description: SpecStory Lore - mine your SpecStory coding histories...
argument-hint: "Enter = guided setup · or plain English, e.g. 'last 30 days, just show candidates'"
allowed-tools: Bash, Read, Write, AskUserQuestion
license: Apache-2.0
hooks:
  PreToolUse:
    - matcher: "ExitPlanMode"
      hooks:
        - type: command
          command: "node \"${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/hooks/validate-plan.mjs\""
---
```

**The hook:** `scripts/hooks/validate-plan.mjs` is a PreToolUse enforcer that **denies any ExitPlanMode call whose plan body does not contain**:
1. The marker `<!-- PASS-THROUGH FORGE PLAN`
2. The sentinel `=== dossiers above: N ===` as the final line
3. At least N `### ` dossier card headers matching the sentinel count

This enforces **LAW 1** (failure mode #3): no summarizing away the evidence.

### Three LAWs (Output Contract, in SKILL.md)

**LAW 1 - DOSSIERS BEFORE QUESTIONS:**
Every candidate decision must be preceded by a message showing full dossiers for every candidate, ending with the sentinel `=== dossiers above: N ===`.

**LAW 2 - PASS-THROUGH RENDERING:**
The agent must emit the engine's visuals verbatim (not summarized): the badge line, dossier cards, theme cards, plan, with every PASS-THROUGH block intact.

**LAW 3 - NARRATE PHASES:**
Before every long-running call, emit a status line (e.g., `📜 indexing BearClaude (253 sessions)…`) so the window always shows what's happening.

## 6. Conventions

### Language & Runtime
- **Node.js ESM** (`.mjs` files)
- **Minimum version:** Node >= 22.5 (for `node:sqlite`)
- **Zero npm dependencies** (only `node:fs`, `node:crypto`, `node:sqlite`, `node:path`, `node:os`)
- **Parallel tools:** if a change needs an npm package, stop and ask first

### File Layout
```
lore/
├── SKILL.md                          ← agent contract (frontmatter + narrative)
├── HOW-IT-WORKS.md                   ← narrative walkthrough (stage by stage)
├── AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md          ← technical reference (this doc)
├── AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md             ← rules for devs working ON lore
├── CONTRIBUTING.md / README.md
├── package.json                      ← {"type": "module", "engines": {"node": ">=22.5"}}
├── .claude-plugin/plugin.json        ← harness metadata
├── scripts/
│   ├── mine-skills.mjs               ← CLI entry (thin dispatcher)
│   ├── deep-mine.workflow.js         ← Claude Code: Workflow script for Phase C (miner + verifier)
│   ├── theme-sweep.workflow.js       ← Claude Code: Workflow script for Phase 2b′ (thematic lenses)
│   ├── hooks/
│   │   └── validate-plan.mjs         ← PreToolUse hook: LAW 1 enforcement
│   └── lib/
│       ├── patterns.mjs              ← format grammar + classifiers
│       ├── parse.mjs                 ← pure transcript parsing (no I/O)
│       ├── discover.mjs              ← file discovery + stable project ID
│       ├── db.mjs                    ← SQLite schema + migrations
│       ├── indexer.mjs               ← incremental indexing
│       ├── report.mjs                ← corroboration queries + scoring
│       ├── beats.mjs                 ← span export, sampling, dossier cache
│       └── forged.mjs                ← registry (provenance + drift)
├── fixtures/                         ← synthetic transcripts per provider form factor
│   ├── projA/.specstory/history/     ← Claude Code modern + legacy formats
│   ├── projB/.specstory/history/     ← Codex formats
│   ├── projC/.specstory/history/     ← Cursor + semantic channel (themes)
│   ├── provider-*/.specstory/history/← provider-specific format coverage
│   └── golden/forge-plan.md          ← golden file (executable spec)
└── tests/
    └── engine.test.mjs               ← 29+ node:test cases (npm test)
```

### Naming Conventions
- **command heads** - lowercase, hyphenated: `git status`, `go build`, `./scripts/run.sh`
- **intent signatures** - `verb:keyword`: `build:run`, `write:commit`, `fix:divergence`
- **cluster keys** - format-specific:
  - gram: `"git status ▸ git add ▸ git commit"` (n-grams joined with ▸)
  - intent: `"write:commit"` (intent_sig)
  - corr: `"write:commit × git status ▸ git add ▸ git commit"` (intent_sig × gram)
  - meta: detector id like `"read-only-diagnosis"`
  - theme: `"freeze-first"` or `"theme:freeze-first"` (stable theme id)
- **session ids** - `project_id/filename` (e.g., `stoa/2026-05-01_10-00-00Z-can-we-run-a.md`)
- **beat keys** - `session_id#ord` (stable across re-indexing, survives file moves)

### Linting & Formatting
- **No em dashes** anywhere (docs, comments, engine output) - use " - " instead
- **Conventional commits** with a why-body: `type(scope): subject`
- **Fixtures are the spec** - new parsing claims need fixture coverage
- **PARSER_VERSION** bump when behavior changes (auto re-parse on next `index`)

### Testing
```bash
npm test                    # 29+ cases via node:test (no test framework deps)
UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 npm test   # regenerate fixtures/golden/forge-plan.md if layout changes
```

Test command in package.json:
```json
"scripts": {
  "test": "node --test tests/*.test.mjs"
}
```

**Test structure** (`tests/engine.test.mjs`):
- **Unit tests** - pure `parse.mjs` functions (`headsFrom`, `extractShellBlock`, `parseSessionFile`, `intentSig`)
- **Integration tests** - index fixtures → assert multi-agent tags, corroborated pairs, cross-project portability
- **Idempotency tests** - index twice (second skipped), `--force` (replace, not duplicate), `prune` (no orphans)
- **Phase C tests** - stratified export, fingerprint stability, dossier cache roundtrip

### Plugin Metadata (`.claude-plugin/plugin.json`)
```json
{

  "displayName": "SpecStory Lore",
  "version": "3.9.0",
  "description": "Mine your SpecStory coding histories...",
  "author": {"name": "SpecStory", "url": "https://github.com/specstoryai"},

  "license": "Apache-2.0",
  "keywords": ["skills", "specstory", "mining", "agent-skills", ...]
}
```

### User Invocation → Execution Flow

**In Claude Code:**
```
/lore [args]
  ↓
Claude Code framework discovers skill at ~/.agents/skills/lore or ~/.claude/skills/lore
  ↓
SKILL.md frontmatter parsed:
  - name: lore
  - allowed-tools: Bash, Read, Write, AskUserQuestion
  - hooks: PreToolUse on ExitPlanMode → validate-plan.mjs
  ↓
Agent executes SKILL.md narrative (Steps 0–6):
  Step 0.25: if no args, ask(Scope / Window / Goal)
  Step 0.5:  interpret args → engine flags
  Step 1:    Bash: node scripts/mine-skills.mjs index --dir ...
             Bash: node scripts/mine-skills.mjs report ...
  Step 2:    agent synthesizes candidates from evidence
  Step 2b:   agent verifies each candidate (opens refs, reads spans)
  Step 2b′:  theme sweep (agent spawns subagents for 6 thematic lenses)
  Step 2c:   deep-mine (Workflow + subagents, or sequential)
  Step 3:    enter plan mode, present curation via ExitPlanMode
             PreToolUse hook: DENY if plan ≠ engine-rendered artifact
  Step 4:    on approval, forge each skill (Write files to ~/.agents/skills/<name>)
             Register via: Bash: node scripts/mine-skills.mjs forged add ...
  Step 5:    privacy scrub (no secrets in SKILL.md)
  Step 6:    report what was forged
             Bash: node scripts/mine-skills.mjs runs add --summary "..."
```

**In other harnesses (Codex, Cursor, Gemini):**
- Skill auto-discovered from `~/.agents/skills/lore` or harness-specific dir
- No ExitPlanMode or plan mode → fallback path:
  - Agent emits dossier message with sentinel
  - Ask via numbered list (not single-select)
  - LAW 1 check: prior message ends with `=== dossiers above: N ===`
  - Same SKILL.md narrative, degrades gracefully

### Repository Install (Live Clone)
```bash

~/.agents/skills/lore → symlink to ~/getspecstory/lore

# Fan-out per harness
~/.claude/skills/lore → symlink to ~/.agents/skills/lore
~/.codex/skills/lore → symlink to ~/.agents/skills/lore

# A git pull in ~/getspecstory updates every harness instantly (symlinks, no copies)
```

## Summary: Why This Architecture for /workthreads

The /lore pattern is optimal for /workthreads because:

1. **Deterministic beats** - a universal model for mining ANY agent interaction (text spans + outcome labels)
2. **Local-only engine** - parses once, caches patterns in SQLite, the agent only reads digested evidence
3. **Incremental + idempotent** - fingerprints ensure re-runs are cheap and safe
4. **Registry memory** - forged skills are tracked, drift-detected, updated (never duplicated)
5. **Multi-agent support** - one parser works for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini, etc. (provider headers match generically)
6. **Harness-portable** - the skill degrades gracefully from plan mode (Claude Code) to sentinel-proven fallback (everywhere else)

**Mirror this pattern for /workthreads:** same module structure, same beats model, same registry discipline, same "evidence export → agent judges" boundary. Replace "coding histories" with "work threads" (Slack, GitHub, Asana, whatever) and the architecture stays the same.

## Step 1 — The analog, mapped (`/lore`)

The pattern is **deterministic engine + agent synthesis**, and it's the thing to mirror:

- **Engine** (`scripts/mine-skills.mjs` + `scripts/lib/*.mjs`, pure Node ESM, **zero deps**, Node ≥22.5): parses `.specstory/history/*.md` into **beats** — `intent → method → outcome`, where the *outcome* is labeled for free from the user's *next* turn (regex classifiers: ✓ success / ✗ corrected / · neutral / end). Beats + n-grams + meta-hits land in a SQLite corpus at `~/.specstory/lore.db`, incrementally and idempotently (fingerprint = size+mtime+`PARSER_VERSION`).
- **"Local-only" / deterministic** = the engine is pure parse+SQL, no network, no API keys, byte-reproducible. The only LLM step is the *agent* reading **exported evidence** (never raw transcripts) to name/judge.
- **"Beats are deterministic"** = the parse→index→report→export pipeline is fixed code; the agent supplies judgment downstream. There's no explicit state enum — phases are driven by the SKILL.md contract.
- **Output**: `/lore` *forges skills* (SKILL.md packages), with a registry (`forged` table) for drift/dedup, and a strict **output contract** (3 LAWs, a PreToolUse hook enforcing evidence-before-questions).
- **Conventions**: `.mjs` ESM, no deps, no em dashes, `node --test tests/*.test.mjs`, **fixtures are the spec**, golden file, conventional commits, `PARSER_VERSION` bumps on parser changes.

## The pivotal finding: yes, the beats approach fits — but the *target* changes

`/lore` scores beats for **recurrence/regularity** to find *reproducible procedures*. `/workthreads` wants something different: group beats into **threads of work** (a line of work on the same topic/files/intent across sessions) and assign each a **lifecycle state**. The good news: the beats already carry exactly the signals you need —

- **NEW** = a thread whose earliest beats fall inside the window.
- **OPEN** = recent activity, no terminal ✓, or unresolved ✗ corrected beats.
- **CLOSED (recently)** = last activity ended in ✓ success and has gone quiet.

So `/workthreads` is plausibly a *re-targeting* of `/lore`'s **themes/corroboration** channels toward "threads + status" instead of "skills," reusing the same deterministic parser and the same evidence-export → agent-judges boundary. That's the core "same vs. deliberately different" delta — and it's the first thing to lock before I draft the goal/DoD.

**How should /workthreads relate to /lore's engine and corpus?**

Options:
- **Reuse lore's engine + corpus** - New /workthreads skill that reads the same beats corpus (~/.specstory/lore.db) and adds a thread-detection + lifecycle layer. DRY — builds on the proven, tested parser; less code; but the build touches/depends on lore.
- **Standalone, mirror lore** - Self-contained workthreads/ skill with its own engine + own SQLite, independent of lore. The most literal 'similar architecture'; fully self-contained (cleaner to gate); but duplicates the parser.
- **Extend /lore itself** - Add a workthreads mode/subcommand inside the existing lore skill — no new skill. Maximal reuse; but couples two distinct purposes and mutates a shipped skill.

**How should a 'thread' and its open/closed/new status be determined?**

Options:
- **Deterministic clusters + lifecycle** - Engine clusters related beats into threads (by intent/theme/files) and derives NEW/OPEN/CLOSED from temporal + outcome signals; the agent labels/judges from exported evidence. Stays true to lore's deterministic-engine boundary.
- **Agent-clustered (semantic)** - Engine just exports beats; the agent groups sessions into threads and judges status. More flexible / better at fuzzy topics, but less deterministic and harder for a gate to verify.
- **Per-session, simple** - Treat each session as a thread; status from recency + last outcome. Simplest and fully deterministic, but coarse — won't merge a thread that spans multiple sessions.

**What should /workthreads produce?**

Options:
- **Thread digest report** - Renders New / Open / Recently-closed sections, each thread with evidence refs, last-activity date, and a status rationale; shown in chat and saved to a file. No installed skills.
- **Installed artifacts (lore-style)** - Persist thread artifacts the way lore forges skill packages (with a registry/drift tracking). Heavier; matches lore most closely but may be more than 'find threads' needs.
- **Chat only** - Present the threads in chat, save nothing to disk. Lightest; but nothing durable to diff or track over time.

Good question — that "what do you want to do" prompt is `/lore`'s **guided start** (Step 0.25), which fires when you run `/lore` with no arguments. It asks **three** questions in one round — **Scope**, **Window**, and **Goal** — and the *Goal* one is the menu you're remembering. Here's the full picture, straight from its `SKILL.md`.

## The guided-start round (bare `/lore`)

**1. Scope** — which histories to mine:
- This project (cwd's `.specstory/history`, auto-detects nested histories) — *recommended*
- All my repos under a folder (scans a parent dir, cross-project mode)
- Just the existing corpus (skip re-indexing, use what's already in `~/.specstory/lore.db`)

**2. Window** — time range: All time *(recommended)* · Last 30 days · Last 90 days.

**3. Goal** — *this is the "what do you want to do" menu*:
- **Find & forge skills** *(recommended)* — the full pipeline: mine → judge → curate → write installed `SKILL.md` skills.
- **Just show me candidates** — mine and judge, render the dossiers, then **stop** (no forging). A dry run.
- **Status / what has Lore done** — show the activity journal (what's been indexed/forged), nothing else.
- **Reset my lore** — wipe the corpus (destructive, confirms first).

## Plus more modes via plain English (not in the 4-option menu, but available)

If you *type* intent instead of taking the guided menu, `/lore` also does:
- **Skills inventory** — "what skills do I have" → lists your forged skills with registry health + every other skill found in your harness dirs.
- **Resume curation** — "pick up where we left off" → re-renders the last saved plan against the current corpus (no re-mining).
- **Filtered mining** — by kind (`cmd` runbooks / `meta` ways-of-working / corroborated), by topic substring ("about supabase"), or by frequency ("did it 10+ times").

So the mental model: **one skill, several modes**, with *forge skills* as the headline mode and *show candidates / status / inventory / resume / reset* as the others. The engine (parse→corpus→evidence) is shared across all of them; the "Goal" just changes how far down the pipeline it goes and what it emits.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-22 18:45:22Z)**_

Great question, and it's the right one to settle before anything else. Based on having both models in my head now, here's my honest read — but first I want to **disentangle two things hiding inside "subcommand of the lore skill,"** because they have opposite answers:

1. **Engine subcommand** — a new `threads` command in the shared engine (`mine-skills.mjs threads …`), reading the same beats corpus. 
2. **Skill mode** — another entry in lore's SKILL.md "Goal" menu, under the same `/lore` skill surface.

My take: **yes to #1, no to #2.** Share the engine; split the skill.

## Why share the engine

The corpus already holds *exactly* what threads needs — beats with intent, outcome (✓/✗/·/end), recency, session, and a themes channel. Thread detection is just a new analytical lens over those beats, the same way `corroboration` and `themes` are lenses today. Forking the deterministic parser into a second skill would duplicate the hardest, most-tested, most-fragile code (the multi-provider transcript parser, `PARSER_VERSION`, fixtures) for zero benefit. So the engine layer should absolutely be reused — in that sense workthreads *is* a new subcommand.

## Why split the skill surface

This is where "mode of lore" works against you:

| Concern | Mode of `/lore` | Separate `/workthreads` |
|---|---|---|
| **Triggering/discovery** | One `description` must cover "forge skills" *and* "what am I in the middle of." The harness picks skills by that description — bundling two intents blurs it. A user asking "what's my open work?" won't think *lore*. | Its own description matches its own intent. Clean triggering. |
| **Output contract** | lore's SKILL.md is 33KB with 3 LAWs, a PreToolUse hook, and named failure modes — all about *forging skills with evidence*. Threads has a *different* contract (a digest; no forge plan, no forged-registry drift). Cramming it in risks weakening lore's hard-won discipline. | Its own, focused contract. lore's LAWs stay pristine. |
| **Context cost** | Every `/lore` invocation loads the threads contract too, and vice-versa. | Each skill loads only what it needs. |
| **DeadReckon build safety** | The run would edit lore's SKILL.md, engine, tests, **and the golden file** — touching the strict output contract under an unattended gate. Higher risk. | A contained new skill + one additive engine subcommand. Far cleaner to gate. |

## The crux is a product-positioning bet

The one scenario where "mode of lore" wins: if your product vision is that **lore is *the* unified "point at your histories and ask" surface** — not "the skill-forge" but "the histories lens" — then threads is just another Goal, and you'd rewrite lore's description to match. That's a legitimate direction. But today lore is positioned and named as the *skill-forging* tool, and threads is a genuinely different value prop (a standup/triage view of work-in-progress). On the current positioning, separate wins.

## My recommendation

**A sibling `/workthreads` skill that reuses lore's engine** — add a `threads` subcommand to the shared `mine-skills.mjs` (over the same corpus), and give workthreads its own slim SKILL.md with a thread-digest contract. Max reuse of the deterministic substrate, clean discovery, lore's contract untouched, and a contained build the gate can actually verify.

That's essentially the **"Reuse lore's engine + corpus"** option from the question I paused on — so your answer here folds directly into that first decision. If you buy this, the remaining forks are just: how a "thread" + its lifecycle is defined, and what the digest output looks like.

**Given we're reusing lore's engine, what's the build shape for /workthreads?**

Options:
- **threads subcommand + thin sibling skill (Recommended)** - Add scripts/lib/threads.mjs and a `threads` subcommand to lore's existing mine-skills.mjs (one parser, one corpus), plus a new /workthreads SKILL.md that calls it. Purely additive — does NOT touch lore's forge flow, SKILL.md, or golden file, so the gate's no-regression check stays clean.
- **Self-contained skill that imports lore's parser** - A separate workthreads/ dir with its own CLI entry that imports lore's parse/discover/db lib modules. More isolated as a skill, but creates a cross-directory code dependency between the two skills.
- **Standalone with its own parser** - A workthreads/ skill that duplicates the transcript parser — no dependency on lore at all. Most literal mirror and fully isolated, but duplicates the hardest, most-tested code.

**What is a 'thread,' and how is its status (new / open / recently-closed) decided?**

Options:
- **Deterministic clusters + lifecycle (Recommended)** - The engine clusters related beats into threads (by shared intent/theme/files) and derives NEW/OPEN/CLOSED deterministically from temporal + outcome signals (first-seen in window = new; recent + unresolved/no terminal success = open; ended in success and quiet = closed). The agent labels/judges from exported evidence. Stays true to lore's deterministic-engine boundary, and the gate can verify it.
- **Agent-clustered (semantic)** - The engine just exports beats; the agent groups sessions into threads and judges status. More flexible for fuzzy topics, but less deterministic and much harder for the gate to verify.
- **Per-session, simple** - Treat each session (or file) as a thread; status from recency + last outcome. Simplest and fully deterministic, but coarse — won't merge one line of work spread across several sessions.

**What should /workthreads produce as output?**

Options:
- **Thread digest saved to a file (Recommended)** - Renders three sections — New / Open / Recently-closed — each thread with evidence refs, last-activity date, and a status rationale; shown in chat AND written to a report file. The saved file gives the deadreckon gate something concrete to check.
- **Tracked thread registry (lore-style)** - A persistent threads table with drift/dedup like lore's forged registry, so threads are tracked across runs. Mirrors lore's registry discipline but is more machinery to build and verify.
- **Chat only** - Present the threads in chat and save nothing. Simplest output, but nothing lands on disk — which weakens what the deadreckon gate can independently confirm.


**Answer:** threads subcommand + thin sibling skill (Recommended), Deterministic clusters + lifecycle (Recommended), Thread digest saved to a file (Recommended)

## Proposed DEFINITION OF DONE (DeadReckon step 3 — the part that matters)

Each line is meant to compile to an executable check:

1. **Runs** — `node scripts/mine-skills.mjs threads --db <scratch.db>` exits 0 and prints a digest with `New`, `Open`, and `Recently closed` sections.
2. **No regressions** — the existing suite still passes: `node --test tests/*.test.mjs` exits 0 (the safety net).
3. **New behavior, concrete cases** — new tests assert against fixtures that: (a) one line of work spanning **multiple sessions** merges into a **single** thread; (b) a thread ending in ✓ and quiet past the window → **CLOSED**; (c) recent activity with an unresolved ✗ / no terminal ✓ → **OPEN**; (d) first-seen in window → **NEW**. Test run exits 0 including these.
4. **Deterministic** — running `threads` twice on the same corpus yields **byte-identical** output (diff exits 0); confirms no LLM/nondeterminism in the engine path.
5. **Saved artifact** — a run writes a report file containing the three section headers; a check asserts the file exists with those sections.
6. **Conventions/parity** — **zero** new dependencies (package.json deps unchanged); no em dashes in new files; new files are Node ESM under `scripts/lib` + `tests/`, mirroring lore's layout.

```text
=== threads_check.sh ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# deadreckon acceptance helper: exercises the `threads` subcommand against a
# deterministic scratch corpus built from the repo fixtures. Covers criteria 1, 4, 5.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd)"
LORE="$ROOT/lore"
cd "$LORE"

TMP="$(mktemp -d)"
DB="$TMP/scratch.db"
R1="$TMP/run1.txt"
R2="$TMP/run2.txt"
OUTFILE="$TMP/report.md"
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# Build a deterministic scratch corpus from the repo fixtures (no network, no LLM).
node scripts/mine-skills.mjs index --projects fixtures --db "$DB" >/dev/null

# Criterion 1: threads exits 0 and the digest carries the three section headers.
node scripts/mine-skills.mjs threads --db "$DB" >"$R1"
for h in "New" "Open" "Recently closed"; do
  grep -qF "$h" "$R1" || { echo "digest missing section header: $h"; exit 1; }
done

# Criterion 4: deterministic - two runs on the same corpus are byte-identical.
node scripts/mine-skills.mjs threads --db "$DB" >"$R2"
cmp -s "$R1" "$R2" || { echo "threads output is not byte-identical across runs"; exit 1; }

# Criterion 5: --out writes a report file carrying the three section headers.
node scripts/mine-skills.mjs threads --db "$DB" --out "$OUTFILE" >/dev/null
[ -f "$OUTFILE" ] || { echo "threads --out did not write a report file"; exit 1; }
for h in "New" "Open" "Recently closed"; do
  grep -qF "$h" "$OUTFILE" || { echo "report file missing section header: $h"; exit 1; }
done

echo "threads acceptance checks passed"

=== no_em_dash.sh ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# deadreckon acceptance helper: fails if any new or modified lore source file
# (.mjs/.js/.md) contains an em dash (U+2014). Covers part of criterion 6.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd)"
cd "$ROOT"

EM=$(printf '\xe2\x80\x94')   # UTF-8 bytes for the em dash character
status=0
files=$( { git diff --name-only HEAD -- lore; git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -- lore; } 2>/dev/null | sort -u )

while IFS= read -r f; do
  [ -n "$f" ] || continue
  case "$f" in
    *.mjs|*.js|*.md) ;;
    *) continue ;;
  esac
  [ -f "$f" ] || continue
  if grep -qF "$EM" "$f"; then
    echo "em dash found in: $f"
    status=1
  fi
done <<EOF
$files
EOF

exit $status
```

#!/usr/bin/env node
// deadreckon acceptance helper (run-INDEPENDENT classification check).
//
// This file lives under .deadreckon (gate-owned, gitignored, NOT in the coding
// worktree), so the coding run never sees it and cannot teach to it. It builds
// its own synthetic corpus with KNOWN thread lifecycles, dated relative to the
// real current date, then asserts `threads --json` classifies each correctly.
//
// Known threads (each keyed by a distinctive file token):
//   WIDGET_ALPHA  -> CLOSED : two sessions (firstseen ~20d, last ~13d), last beat success, then quiet
//   WIDGET_BETA   -> OPEN   : two sessions (firstseen ~16d, last ~2d), last beat an unresolved correction
//   WIDGET_GAMMA  -> NEW    : one session (~1d ago), first activity inside the new-window
import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process'
import { mkdtempSync, mkdirSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os'
import { join } from 'node:path'

const ENGINE = 'lore/scripts/mine-skills.mjs'   // relative to {working_dir} (repo root)
const fail = (m) => { console.error('threads-classify: ' + m); process.exit(1) }

// YYYY-MM-DD for "n days ago" from now.
const ymd = (days) => new Date(Date.now() - days * 86400000).toISOString().slice(0, 10)

let uid = 0
const SESS = (date, slug, turns) => {
  uid++
  const uuid = `cccccccc-0000-4000-8000-${String(uid).padStart(12, '0')}`
  let s = `## ${date} 09:00:00Z\n\n<!-- Claude Code Session ${uuid} (${date}_09-00-00Z) -->\n`
  for (const t of turns) {
    s += `\n_**User**_\n\n${t.user}\n\n---\n`
    if (t.cmd) {
      s += `\n_**Agent (claude-opus-4-20250514)**_\n\nTool use: **Bash** ${t.desc || 'work'}\n\n\`${t.cmd}\`\n\nResult:\n\n\`\`\`\n${t.result || ''}\n\`\`\`\n`
    }
  }
  return { name: `${date}_09-00-00Z-${slug}.md`, body: s }
}

// Build the corpus.
const root = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'wt-classify-'))
const hist = join(root, '.specstory', 'history')
mkdirSync(hist, { recursive: true })

const files = [
  // CLOSED: WIDGET_ALPHA across two sessions; last session resolves in success.
  SESS(ymd(20), 'begin-widget-alpha', [
    { user: 'begin the WIDGET_ALPHA implementation', desc: 'create alpha module', cmd: 'touch src/WIDGET_ALPHA.swift' },
  ]),
  SESS(ymd(13), 'finish-widget-alpha', [
    { user: 'finish the WIDGET_ALPHA implementation', desc: 'build alpha module', cmd: 'swift build src/WIDGET_ALPHA.swift', result: 'Build complete' },
    { user: 'perfect, that works' },
  ]),
  // OPEN: WIDGET_BETA scaffolded long ago, last touched recently and still broken.
  SESS(ymd(16), 'scaffold-widget-beta', [
    { user: 'scaffold the WIDGET_BETA module', desc: 'create beta module', cmd: 'touch src/WIDGET_BETA.swift' },
  ]),
  SESS(ymd(2), 'fix-widget-beta', [
    { user: 'fix the WIDGET_BETA crash', desc: 'patch beta module', cmd: 'swift build src/WIDGET_BETA.swift', result: 'crash' },
    { user: 'no, it still crashes' },
  ]),
  // NEW: WIDGET_GAMMA started within the last day.
  SESS(ymd(1), 'start-widget-gamma', [
    { user: 'start the WIDGET_GAMMA prototype', desc: 'create gamma module', cmd: 'touch src/WIDGET_GAMMA.swift' },
  ]),
]
for (const f of files) writeFileSync(join(hist, f.name), f.body)

// Index + run threads --json against the synthetic corpus.
const db = join(root, 'corpus.db')
try {
  execFileSync('node', [ENGINE, 'index', '--dir', hist, '--db', db], { stdio: ['ignore', 'ignore', 'inherit'] })
} catch (e) { fail('engine index failed: ' + (e.message || e)) }

let out
try {
  out = execFileSync('node', [ENGINE, 'threads', '--db', db, '--json'], { encoding: 'utf8' })
} catch (e) { fail('`threads --json` failed (subcommand missing or errored): ' + (e.message || e)) }

let threads
try {
  const parsed = JSON.parse(out)
  threads = Array.isArray(parsed) ? parsed : parsed.threads
  if (!Array.isArray(threads)) throw new Error('expected an array (or {threads:[...]})')
} catch (e) { fail('`threads --json` did not emit parseable JSON to stdout: ' + (e.message || e)) }

const STATUSES = new Set(['new', 'open', 'closed'])
const find = (token) => threads.filter(t => JSON.stringify(t).includes(token))

for (const [token, want] of [['WIDGET_ALPHA', 'closed'], ['WIDGET_BETA', 'open'], ['WIDGET_GAMMA', 'new']]) {
  const hits = find(token)
  if (hits.length !== 1) fail(`expected exactly ONE thread containing ${token}, found ${hits.length} (clustering/merge wrong)`)
  const st = String(hits[0].status || '').toLowerCase()
  if (!STATUSES.has(st)) fail(`thread for ${token} has invalid status ${JSON.stringify(hits[0].status)} (want one of new|open|closed)`)
  if (st !== want) fail(`thread for ${token} classified ${st}, expected ${want}`)
}

// Separation: the ALPHA (closed) thread must not have absorbed BETA/GAMMA work.
const alpha = find('WIDGET_ALPHA')[0]
const alphaStr = JSON.stringify(alpha)
if (alphaStr.includes('WIDGET_BETA') || alphaStr.includes('WIDGET_GAMMA')) {
  fail('the WIDGET_ALPHA thread absorbed other threads (over-merged)')
}

console.log('threads classification check passed (alpha=closed, beta=open, gamma=new, threads separated)')

# Goal: `threads` subcommand + `/workthreads` skill (mirror lore)

Build a `threads` subcommand for the SpecStory lore engine plus a thin sibling
`/workthreads` skill, **mirroring lore's architecture and conventions**, working
inside the `lore/` directory of this repo.

## Engine

Add `lore/scripts/lib/threads.mjs` and wire a `threads` subcommand into
`lore/scripts/mine-skills.mjs`. It reads the **same beats corpus** the existing
engine builds (SQLite via `node:sqlite`, the `--db` flag, the existing
sessions/beats/commands/grams tables) and clusters related beats into **work
threads**, using ONLY existing corpus columns — **no schema change, no
`PARSER_VERSION` bump, no LLM or network call in the engine path.**

- **Clustering:** the primary signal is **shared touched-files** — sessions/beats
  that touch the same file belong to the same thread — reinforced by shared intent
  keyword and command grams. Merge a line of work across multiple sessions into ONE
  thread.
- **Lifecycle status** (assign exactly one per thread; evaluate in this precedence
  order, all relative to the current date):
  1. **closed** — the thread's most recent labeled outcome is **success** and it has
     been quiet for **≥ 3 days**, with last activity **within 30 days** (shown under
     "Recently closed").
  2. **new** — the thread's **first** activity is **within the last 7 days**.
  3. **open** — otherwise, if it has activity **within the last 14 days**.
  (Threads older/quieter than the above may be omitted from the digest.)

## Output

- A human **digest** to stdout with exactly these section headers, in this order:
  `New`, `Open`, `Recently closed`. Each thread shows evidence refs
  (`path:line`), last-activity date, and a one-line status rationale. Always print
  all three headers even when a section is empty.
- `--out <file>` also writes that digest to a file.
- `--json` prints **only** machine-readable JSON to stdout (nothing else): an array
  of thread objects (or `{ "threads": [ ... ] }`), each with a `status` field whose
  value is exactly one of `"new" | "open" | "closed"`, plus the list of files the
  thread touched (so a thread is identifiable by the files in its evidence).
- **Determinism:** output is byte-identical across two runs on the same corpus
  (stable sort, no wall-clock timestamps embedded in the body).

## Fixtures + tests

Add fixtures under `lore/fixtures` (REAL SpecStory transcript bytes following the
existing Claude Code format already used in `lore/fixtures/projA`) encoding threads
with known lifecycle states, and add `lore/tests/threads.test.mjs` (Node's built-in
`node --test`, mirroring `lore/tests/engine.test.mjs`) asserting: a line of work
spanning multiple sessions merges into ONE thread; a success-then-quiet thread is
**closed**; a recent unresolved thread is **open**; a first-seen-in-window thread is
**new**. The full `node --test tests/*.test.mjs` (existing + new) must pass.

## Skill surface

Add `lore/workthreads/SKILL.md` (agentskills.io format, mirroring
`lore/SKILL.md`'s frontmatter shape) with `name: workthreads`, a `description`,
`allowed-tools`, and a body that drives the flow and instructs calling the
`threads` subcommand (e.g. `node <skill-dir>/../scripts/mine-skills.mjs threads`),
with a lore-style guided start (Scope / Window / Goal, where Goal = all threads /
just open / recently closed / status).

## Conventions (mirror lore exactly)

Node ESM `.mjs`; **zero npm dependencies**; Node >= 22.5; **no em dashes anywhere**;

But the goal currently jumps straight into mechanics with **no statement of what `/workthreads` is *for*** — the user, the problem, the value. That gap matters here specifically because the coder is writing a **SKILL.md**, whose `description` (triggering) and body (voice, the guided-start framing, the per-thread rationale text) all depend on understanding the *intent*. Without it, you can get a mechanically-correct skill that's purpose-confused — a digest that's technically right but doesn't read like it's answering a real question.

It won't add any gate checks (purpose is judgment, not a verifiable command), but it'll meaningfully sharpen the output where the gate can't reach. So: add it.

Here's the section I'd prepend, right after the title:

> ## Purpose (what `/workthreads` is for)
>
> The user works with AI coding agents, so their SpecStory histories accumulate a running record of everything they've worked on. `/workthreads` reads those histories and shows the **current state of their work-in-progress as threads of work**: what they recently **started**, what is still **open** (in progress or left unresolved), and what they **recently closed** (wrapped up successfully). The job it does for the user is fast re-orientation — *"what am I in the middle of, what did I leave unfinished, and what did I just finish?"* — whether returning after time away, prepping a standup, or deciding what to pick back up next.
>
> It is the sibling lens to `/lore` over the **same corpus**: where `/lore` mines for reproducible *procedures* to forge into skills, `/workthreads` tracks *lines of work and their lifecycle*. Everything below serves that goal — the engine and digest exist to answer that question accurately and at a glance.

A couple of optional sharpeners we could fold in if they match your intent (tell me):

_**User (2026-06-22 19:44:05Z)**_

ok... and why not the 6-child fanout?? that seems like it could be useful given all the gates that need checking, no? or is that not how it works

---

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-22 19:44:48Z)**_

Fair challenge — but it rests on a misconception about what the children do, and it's worth getting right.

**The fanout parallelizes *coding*, not *gate-checking*.** `dr-gate` runs **once, at the end, on the final merged worktree** — in every mode. The 13 checks aren't divided among children; there's no speedup or extra coverage from more agents on the checking side. Full-plan's children are a **planner decomposing the goal into N sub-tasks**, each child building a slice in its own worktree, then the slices get **merged**. So more children = more parallel *construction*, then a merge step — the verification is identical either way.

**Why that's the wrong fit for this task specifically:** `/workthreads` is *one tightly-coupled module*, not separable work:
- `threads.test.mjs` depends on the `--json` schema, which depends on `threads.mjs`, which depends on the fixtures' format and the lifecycle windows. Split those across 6 independent agents and you get **integration seams** — child A's status field names don't match child B's test assertions, child C's fixtures don't exercise the windows child A implemented. Merging divergent takes on *one coherent design* usually costs more than it saves.
- The total surface is a few hundred lines across a handful of files. Six agents would mostly **contend on the same files**, not work in parallel.
- Net: full-plan adds a planner + 6 children + a merge (more time, more failure surface) and buys **zero** extra gate rigor.

**When fanout *does* shine:** broad, weakly-coupled scope — "add 6 independent provider parsers," "migrate 20 files," "build 5 unrelated endpoints." Separable slices, clean merges. Not this.

**If what you actually want is more scrutiny here, the relevant lever is `--mode review`, not full-plan.** Review = a coder builds, then an *independent reviewer agent* critiques and the coder revises, *before* the gate. That's adversarial quality pressure on one cohesive change — which fits a "lots of gates, want it right" instinct far better than parallel decomposition.

So your options:
- **`--mode run`** (recommended) — one coder, gated. Cohesive task, simplest, the gate is your check.
- **`--mode review`** — adds an independent reviewer pass before the gate. A bit more time; useful if you want a built-in critic catching issues the gate's binary checks won't (e.g., does the SKILL.md actually read well, is the digest genuinely useful).
- **full-plan** — skip it here; wrong tool for one tightly-coupled module.

Want to go with `run`, or upgrade to `review` for the extra critic? Either uses the same goal + the same 13-check gate.

              `lore/scripts/mine-skills.mjs`. It reads the **same beats corpus** the existing
              engine builds (SQLite via `node:sqlite`, the `--db` flag, the existing
              sessions/beats/commands/grams tables) and clusters related beats into **work
              threads**, using ONLY existing corpus columns — **no schema change, no
              `PARSER_VERSION` bump, no LLM or network call in the engine path.**
              
              - **Clustering:** the primary signal is **shared touched-files** — sessions/beats
              that touch the same file belong to the same thread — reinforced by shared intent
              keyword and command grams. Merge a line of work across multiple sessions into ONE
              thread.
              - **Lifecycle status** (assign exactly one per thread; evaluate in this precedence
              order, all relative to the current date):
              1. **closed** — the thread's most recent labeled outcome is **success** and it has
              been quiet for **≥ 3 days**, with last activity **within 30 days** (shown under
              "Recently closed").
              2. **new** — the thread's **first** activity is **within the last 7 days**.
              3. **open** — otherwise, if it has activity **within the last 14 days**.
              (Threads older/quieter than the above may be omitted from the digest.)
              
              ## Output
              
              - A human **digest** to stdout with exactly these section headers, in this order:
              `New`, `Open`, `Recently closed`. Each thread shows evidence refs
              (`path:line`), last-activity date, and a one-line status rationale. Always print
              all three headers even when a section is empty.
              - `--out <file>` also writes that digest to a file.
              - `--json` prints **only** machine-readable JSON to stdout (nothing else): an array
              of thread objects (or `{ "threads": [ ... ] }`), each with a `status` field whose
              value is exactly one of `"new" | "open" | "closed"`, plus the list of files the
              thread touched.

goal         : # Goal: `threads` subcommand + `/workthreads` skill (mirror lore)
               
               ## Purpose
               
               `/workthreads` reads the user's SpecStory histories and shows their work-in-progress
               as **threads**: what they recently **started** (new), what is still **open**/unresolved,
               and what they **recently closed**. It answers, at a glance, *"what am I in the middle
               of, what's unfinished, what did I just finish?"* - for re-orienting after time away or
               prepping a standup. It is the sibling lens to `/lore` over the **same corpus**: `/lore`
               mines reproducible *procedures* to forge into skills; `/workthreads` tracks *lines of
               work and their lifecycle*.

Found it — and **it's a bug in deadreckon, not in your setup or our contract.** The event log shows the coder run worked for ~17 minutes, then deadreckon's own Rust runtime **panicked**:

```
thread 'tokio-rt-worker' panicked at crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/flight.rs:1017:13:
assertion failed: self.is_char_boundary(new_len)
error: provider flight recorder task failed: task 21 panicked
```

That's a classic **UTF-8 slicing bug**: deadreckon's "flight recorder" (which logs the provider stream) tried to cut a string at a byte offset landing in the *middle of a multi-byte character*, and crashed. Then task-1 (the codex reviewer) got blocked because its dependency died. Two things worth noting: your **repo is untouched** (isolated worktree, source still clean at `b5a5414`), and the **codex reviewer was never the problem** — the coder crashed before handing off.

The most likely controllable trigger: **multi-byte characters in our `goal.md`** — I left em dashes (`—`) and `≥` in the Engine/lifecycle section (ironic, given lore's "no em dashes" rule). The recorder echoes the goal, and those are exactly the chars that break a naive byte-slice. Let me confirm what non-ASCII is in there:

## What to run (in your terminal)

```

The reviewer (codex) was never the problem — the coder crashed before handing off — so it's fine to keep the critic.

## Honest caveat (so you're not surprised)

This is a **deadreckon defect**, not our setup: its flight recorder panics when it slices a recorded string mid-multibyte-character (`flight.rs:1017`, `is_char_boundary` assertion). Stripping our goal's em dashes kills the *controllable* trigger — but the recorder also logs the **agent's own output and tool output**, which we don't control and could contain a multibyte char (an em dash it types, an emoji, a box-drawing char). It crashed at ~17 min into a long first turn, and more recorded output = more chance of hitting it.

**So the retry may sail through, or it may recur.** If it recurs:
1. It's a reportable deadreckon bug — clean repro (panic at `flight.rs:1017` on multibyte content); a newer version than your `0.2.0` may already fix it, so check for an update first.
2. Try `--mode run` (one lane, less recorded output) as a lower-surface fallback.
3. I can add an "emit ASCII-only output" line to the goal (consistent with lore's no-em-dash rule anyway) to cut the chance the *agent* feeds the recorder a multibyte char — I left it out for now to stay under 4k, but it's a quick add if needed.

Also FYI, not today's issue: the run applied a default **`--max-spend $10`** cap (and a 10h wall). On Max that likely reads ~$0 and never trips, but if a long review run ever stops citing spend, add `--max-spend 50`.

Kick off the three commands and send me `deadreckon status` (or `attach`) once it's moving — I'll watch for either the gate verdict or a recurrence of that panic.

## What

`truncate_summary` (`crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/flight.rs`) truncated with
`String::truncate(MAX_SUMMARY_CHARS)`, using the constant as a **byte** index.
`String::truncate` panics when the index is not a UTF-8 char boundary, so any
provider output containing a multibyte character (an em dash, smart quote, emoji,
box-drawing char, ...) whose byte 240 landed mid-character crashed the flight
recorder.

## Impact

The panic killed the coding run, and in orchestration (`--mode review` / `full-plan`)
the whole plan then paused because the child task "failed":

\```
thread 'tokio-rt-worker' panicked at crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/flight.rs:1017:13:
assertion failed: self.is_char_boundary(new_len)
error: provider flight recorder task failed: task 21 panicked with message
       "assertion failed: self.is_char_boundary(new_len)"
\```

Hit on a real `start` run whose goal text contained em dashes; ~17 minutes of
coding work was lost.

## Fix

Truncate by **character**, not byte: `char_indices().nth(MAX_SUMMARY_CHARS)` yields
the byte offset of the Nth char only when more than N chars exist, and that offset
is always a valid boundary. This also makes the behavior match the constant's
`_CHARS` name.

## Tests

Two unit tests in the `flight` module:
- `truncate_summary_handles_multibyte_boundary` - 239 ASCII bytes + em dashes so
  byte 240 falls mid-character; reproduces the old panic, passes with the fix.
- `truncate_summary_keeps_short_strings` - trim + newline-collapse passthrough.

`cargo test --release -p deadreckon-runtime truncate_summary` -> 2 passed.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
gh pr create --repo gregce/deadreckon --base main --head jakelevirne:fix/flight-recorder-utf8-truncation --draft --title "fix(runtime): truncate flight summaries on char boundaries (UTF-8 panic)" --body-file /tmp/dr-pr-body.md 2>&1 | tail -8
```
